    25→def _execute_serial(
    26→    *,
    27→    tasks: dict[int, BatchTask],
    28→    indexes: list[int],
    29→    progress_fn,
    30→    error_log_fn,
    31→    clock_fn,
    32→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
    33→) -> list[int]:
    34→    normalized_indexes: list[int] = []
    35→    seen: set[int] = set()
    36→    for idx in indexes:
    37→        if idx in seen:
    38→            continue
    39→        seen.add(idx)
    40→        if idx not in tasks:
    41→            continue
    42→        normalized_indexes.append(idx)
    43→    if not normalized_indexes:
    44→        return []
    45→    return execute_serial_tasks(
    46→        tasks=tasks,
    47→        indexes=normalized_indexes,
    48→        progress_fn=progress_fn,
    49→        error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
    50→        clock_fn=clock_fn,
    51→        contract_cache=contract_cache,
    52→        emit_progress_fn=_emit_progress,
    53→        record_execution_error_fn=_record_execution_error,
    54→        runner_task_exceptions=_RUNNER_TASK_EXCEPTIONS,
    55→    )
    56→
    57→
    58→def _resolve_parallel_runtime(
    59→    *,
    60→    indexes: list[int],
    61→    max_parallel_workers,
    62→    heartbeat_seconds,
    63→) -> tuple[int, float | None]:
    64→    requested = (
    65→        int(max_parallel_workers)
    66→        if isinstance(max_parallel_workers, int) and max_parallel_workers > 0
    67→        else 8
    68→    )
    69→    max_workers = max(1, min(len(indexes), requested))
    70→    heartbeat = (
    71→        float(heartbeat_seconds)
    72→        if isinstance(heartbeat_seconds, int | float) and heartbeat_seconds > 0
    73→        else None
    74→    )
    75→    return max_workers, heartbeat
    76→
    77→
    78→def _run_parallel_task(
    79→    *,
    80→    idx: int,
    81→    tasks: dict[int, BatchTask],
    82→    progress_fn,
    83→    error_log_fn,
    84→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
    85→    max_workers: int,
    86→    progress_failures: set[int],
    87→    started_at: dict[int, float],
    88→    lock: threading.Lock,
    89→    clock_fn,
    90→) -> int:
    91→    with lock:
    92→        started_at[idx] = float(clock_fn())
    93→    progress_error = _emit_progress(
    94→        progress_fn,
    95→        idx,
    96→        "start",
    97→        None,
    98→        details={"max_workers": max_workers},
    99→        contract_cache=contract_cache,
   100→    )
   101→    if progress_error is not None:
   102→        _record_progress_error(
   103→            idx=idx,
   104→            err=progress_error,
   105→            progress_failures=progress_failures,
   106→            lock=lock,
   107→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   108→        )
   109→    return tasks[idx]()
   110→
   111→
   112→def _queue_parallel_tasks(
   113→    *,
   114→    executor: ThreadPoolExecutor,
   115→    indexes: list[int],
   116→    tasks: dict[int, BatchTask],
   117→    progress_fn,
   118→    error_log_fn,
   119→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
   120→    max_workers: int,
   121→    failures: set[int],
   122→    progress_failures: set[int],
   123→    started_at: dict[int, float],
   124→    lock: threading.Lock,
   125→    clock_fn,
   126→) -> dict:
   127→    futures: dict = {}
   128→    for idx in indexes:
   129→        queue_error = _emit_progress(
   130→            progress_fn,
   131→            idx,
   132→            "queued",
   133→            None,
   134→            details={"max_workers": max_workers},
   135→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
   136→        )
   137→        if queue_error is not None:

   139→                idx=idx,
   140→                err=queue_error,
   141→                progress_failures=progress_failures,
   142→                lock=lock,
   143→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   144→            )
   145→            failures.add(idx)
   146→        futures[
   147→            executor.submit(
   148→                _run_parallel_task,
   149→                idx=idx,
   150→                tasks=tasks,
   151→                progress_fn=progress_fn,
   152→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   153→                contract_cache=contract_cache,
   154→                max_workers=max_workers,
   155→                progress_failures=progress_failures,
   156→                started_at=started_at,
   157→                lock=lock,
   158→                clock_fn=clock_fn,
   159→            )
   160→        ] = idx
   161→    return futures
   162→
   163→
   164→def _complete_parallel_future(
   165→    *,
   166→    future,
   167→    futures: dict,
   168→    progress_fn,
   169→    error_log_fn,
   170→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
   171→    failures: set[int],
   172→    progress_failures: set[int],
   173→    started_at: dict[int, float],
   174→    lock: threading.Lock,
   175→    clock_fn,
   176→) -> None:
   177→    idx = futures[future]
   178→    with lock:
   179→        t0 = started_at.get(idx, float(clock_fn()))
   180→    elapsed = int(max(0.0, clock_fn() - t0))
   181→    try:
   182→        code = future.result()
   183→    except _RUNNER_TASK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   184→        _record_execution_error(
   185→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   186→            failures=failures,
   187→            idx=idx,
   188→            exc=exc,
   189→        )
   190→        done_error = _emit_progress(
   191→            progress_fn,
   192→            idx,
   193→            "done",
   194→            1,
   195→            details={"elapsed_seconds": elapsed},
   196→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
   197→        )
   198→        if done_error is not None:
   199→            _record_progress_error(
   200→                idx=idx,
   201→                err=done_error,
   202→                progress_failures=progress_failures,
   203→                lock=lock,
   204→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   205→            )
   206→        return
   207→
   208→    done_error = _emit_progress(
   209→        progress_fn,
   210→        idx,
   211→        "done",
   212→        code,
   213→        details={"elapsed_seconds": elapsed},
   214→        contract_cache=contract_cache,
   215→    )
   216→    if done_error is not None:
   217→        _record_progress_error(
   218→            idx=idx,
   219→            err=done_error,
   220→            progress_failures=progress_failures,
   221→            lock=lock,
   222→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   223→        )
   224→
   225→    with lock:
   226→        had_progress_failure = idx in progress_failures
   227→    if code != 0 or had_progress_failure:
   228→        failures.add(idx)
   229→
   230→
   231→def _drain_parallel_completions(
   232→    *,
   233→    pending: set,
   234→    futures: dict,
   235→    heartbeat: float | None,
   236→    indexes: list[int],
   237→    progress_fn,
   238→    error_log_fn,
   239→    contract_cache: dict[int, str],
   240→    failures: set[int],
   241→    progress_failures: set[int],
   242→    started_at: dict[int, float],
   243→    lock: threading.Lock,
   244→    clock_fn,
   245→) -> None:
   246→    if heartbeat is None:
   247→        for future in as_completed(pending):
   248→            _complete_parallel_future(
   249→                future=future,
   250→                futures=futures,
   251→                progress_fn=progress_fn,
   252→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   253→                contract_cache=contract_cache,
   254→                failures=failures,
   255→                progress_failures=progress_failures,
   256→                started_at=started_at,
   257→                lock=lock,
   258→                clock_fn=clock_fn,
   259→            )
   260→        return
   261→
   262→    while pending:
   263→        try:
   264→            future = next(as_completed(pending, timeout=heartbeat))
   265→        except FuturesTimeoutError:
   266→            _heartbeat(
   267→                pending,
   268→                futures,
   269→                started_at,
   270→                lock,
   271→                indexes,
   272→                progress_fn,
   273→                clock_fn,
   274→                error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   275→                contract_cache=contract_cache,
   276→            )
   277→            continue
   278→        pending.discard(future)
   279→        _complete_parallel_future(
   280→            future=future,
   281→            futures=futures,
   282→            progress_fn=progress_fn,
   283→            error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   284→            contract_cache=contract_cache,
   285→            failures=failures,
   286→            progress_failures=progress_failures,
   287→            started_at=started_at,
   288→            lock=lock,
   289→            clock_fn=clock_fn,
   290→        )
   291→
   292→
   293→def _heartbeat(
   294→    pending,
   295→    futures,
   296→    started_at,
   297→    lock,
   298→    indexes,
   299→    progress_fn,
   300→    clock_fn,
   301→    *,
   302→    error_log_fn=None,
   303→    contract_cache: dict[int, str] | None = None,
   304→):
   305→    """Build and emit a heartbeat with active/queued batch status."""
   306→    with lock:
   307→        active = sorted(futures[f] for f in pending if futures[f] in started_at)
   308→    active_set = set(active)
   309→    queued = sorted(futures[f] for f in pending if futures[f] not in active_set)
   310→    elapsed = {
   311→        idx: int(max(0.0, clock_fn() - started_at.get(idx, clock_fn())))
   312→        for idx in active
   313→    }
   314→    heartbeat_error = _emit_progress(
   315→        progress_fn,
   316→        -1,
   317→        "heartbeat",
   318→        None,
   319→        details={
   320→            "active_batches": active,
   321→            "queued_batches": queued,
   322→            "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
   323→            "active_count": len(active),
   324→            "queued_count": len(queued),
   325→            "total_count": len(indexes),
   326→        },
   327→        contract_cache=contract_cache,
   328→    )
   329→    if heartbeat_error is not None and callable(error_log_fn):
   330→        try:
   331→            error_log_fn(-1, heartbeat_error)
   332→        except _RUNNER_CALLBACK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   333→            log_best_effort_failure(
   334→                logger,
   335→                "record batch heartbeat failure via callback",
   336→                exc,
   337→            )
   338→
   339→
   340→__all__ = [
   341→    "_complete_parallel_future",
   342→    "_drain_parallel_completions",
   343→    "_execute_serial",
   344→    "_heartbeat",
   345→    "_queue_parallel_tasks",
   346→    "_resolve_parallel_runtime",
   347→    "_run_parallel_task",
   348→]
   349→

   136→def _run_via_subprocess(
   137→    cmd: list[str],
   138→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   139→    state: _RunnerState,

   151→    except deps.timeout_error:

   154→        return _ExecutionResult(code=124, stdout_text="", stderr_text="", timed_out=True)

   160→        return _ExecutionResult(code=127, stdout_text="", stderr_text="", early_return=127)
   161→    except (RuntimeError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive boundary

   166→        return _ExecutionResult(code=1, stdout_text="", stderr_text="", early_return=1)
   167→    finally:

   176→def _resolve_retry_config(deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps) -> _RetryConfig:
   177→    retries_raw = deps.max_retries if isinstance(deps.max_retries, int) else 0
   178→    max_retries = max(0, retries_raw)
   179→    max_attempts = max_retries + 1
   180→    backoff_raw = (
   181→        float(deps.retry_backoff_seconds)
   182→        if isinstance(deps.retry_backoff_seconds, int | float)
   183→        else 0.0
   184→    )
   185→    retry_backoff_seconds = max(0.0, backoff_raw)
   186→    live_log_interval = (
   187→        float(deps.live_log_interval_seconds)
   188→        if isinstance(deps.live_log_interval_seconds, int | float)
   189→        and float(deps.live_log_interval_seconds) > 0
   190→        else 5.0
   191→    )
   192→    stall_seconds = (
   193→        int(deps.stall_after_output_seconds)
   194→        if isinstance(deps.stall_after_output_seconds, int | float)
   195→        and int(deps.stall_after_output_seconds) > 0
   196→        else 0
   197→    )
   198→    use_popen = bool(deps.use_popen_runner) and callable(
   199→        getattr(deps, "subprocess_popen", None)
   200→    )
   201→    return _RetryConfig(
   202→        max_attempts=max_attempts,
   203→        retry_backoff_seconds=retry_backoff_seconds,
   204→        live_log_interval=live_log_interval,
   205→        stall_seconds=stall_seconds,
   206→        use_popen=use_popen,
   207→    )
   208→def _run_batch_attempt(
   209→    *,
   210→    cmd: list[str],
   211→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   212→    output_file: Path,
   213→    log_file: Path,
   214→    log_sections: list[str],
   215→    attempt: int,
   216→    max_attempts: int,
   217→    use_popen: bool,
   218→    live_log_interval: float,
   219→    stall_seconds: int,
   220→) -> tuple[str, _ExecutionResult]:
   221→    header = f"ATTEMPT {attempt}/{max_attempts}\n$ {' '.join(cmd)}"
   222→    started_monotonic = time.monotonic()
   223→    state = _RunnerState(last_stream_activity=started_monotonic)
   224→    ctx = _AttemptContext(
   225→        header=header,
   226→        started_at_iso=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
   227→        started_monotonic=started_monotonic,
   228→        output_file=output_file,
   229→        log_file=log_file,
   230→        log_sections=log_sections,
   231→        safe_write_text_fn=deps.safe_write_text_fn,
   232→    )
   233→    _write_live_snapshot(state, ctx)
   234→    if use_popen:
   235→        result = _run_via_popen(
   236→            cmd,
   237→            deps,
   238→            state,
   239→            ctx,
   240→            live_log_interval,
   241→            stall_seconds,
   242→        )
   243→    else:
   244→        result = _run_via_subprocess(cmd, deps, state, ctx, live_log_interval)
   245→    return header, result
   246→
   247→
   248→def _handle_early_attempt_return(result: _ExecutionResult) -> int | None:
   249→    return result.early_return
   250→
   251→
   252→def _handle_timeout_or_stall(
   253→    *,
   254→    header: str,
   255→    result: _ExecutionResult,
   256→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   257→    output_file: Path,
   258→    log_file: Path,
   259→    log_sections: list[str],
   260→    stall_seconds: int,
   261→) -> int | None:
   262→    if not result.timed_out and not result.stalled:
   263→        return None
   264→    if result.timed_out:
   265→        log_sections.append(
   266→            f"{header}\n\nTIMEOUT after {deps.timeout_seconds}s\n\n"
   267→            f"STDOUT:\n{result.stdout_text}\n\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr_text}\n"
   268→        )
   269→    else:
   270→        log_sections.append(
   271→            f"{header}\n\nSTALL RECOVERY after {stall_seconds}s "
   272→            "of stable output and no stream activity.\n\n"
   273→            f"STDOUT:\n{result.stdout_text}\n\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr_text}\n"
   274→        )
   275→    if _output_file_has_json_payload(output_file):
   276→        recovery_message = (
   277→            "Recovered timed-out batch from JSON output file; "
   278→            "continuing as success."
   279→            if result.timed_out
   280→            else "Recovered stalled batch from JSON output file; "
   281→            "continuing as success."
   282→        )
   283→        log_sections.append(recovery_message)
   284→        deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   285→        return 0
   286→    deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   287→    return 124
   288→
   289→
   290→def _handle_successful_attempt(
   291→    *,
   292→    result: _ExecutionResult,
   293→    output_file: Path,
   294→    log_file: Path,
   295→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   296→    log_sections: list[str],
   297→) -> int | None:
   298→    if result.code != 0:
   299→        return None
   300→    if not output_file.exists():
   301→        log_sections.append("Runner returned 0 but output file is missing.")
   302→    validate_fn = deps.validate_output_fn
   303→    if validate_fn is None:
   304→        validate_fn = _output_file_has_json_payload
   305→    return handle_successful_attempt_core(
   306→        result=result,
   307→        output_file=output_file,
   308→        log_file=log_file,
   309→        deps=deps,
   310→        log_sections=log_sections,
   311→        default_validate_fn=validate_fn,
   312→        monotonic_fn=time.monotonic,
   313→    )
   314→
   315→
   316→def _handle_failed_attempt(
   317→    *,
   318→    result: _ExecutionResult,
   319→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   320→    attempt: int,
   321→    max_attempts: int,
   322→    retry_backoff_seconds: float,
   323→    log_file: Path,
   324→    log_sections: list[str],
   325→) -> int | None:
   326→    combined = f"{result.stdout_text}\n{result.stderr_text}".lower()
   327→    is_transient = any(needle in combined for needle in _TRANSIENT_RUNNER_PHRASES)
   328→    if not is_transient or attempt >= max_attempts:
   329→        deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   330→        return result.code
   331→    delay_seconds = retry_backoff_seconds * (2 ** (attempt - 1))
   332→    log_sections.append(
   333→        "Transient runner failure detected; "
   334→        f"retrying in {delay_seconds:.1f}s (attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_attempts})."
   335→    )
   336→    try:
   337→        if delay_seconds > 0:
   338→            deps.sleep_fn(delay_seconds)
   339→    except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
   340→        log_sections.append(
   341→            f"Retry delay hook failed: {exc} — aborting remaining retries."
   342→        )
   343→        deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   344→        return 1
   345→    return None
   346→
   347→
   348→__all__ = [

   353→    "_resolve_retry_config",
   354→    "_run_batch_attempt",
   355→    "_run_via_popen",
   356→    "_run_via_subprocess",
   357→]

1→"""Shared orchestration bodies for TypeScript coupling phase helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→from typing import Any
     7→
     8→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import LangRuntimeContract
     9→from desloppify.state import Issue
    10→
    11→
    12→def make_boundary_issues(
    13→    single_entries: list[dict],
    14→    path: Path,
    15→    graph: dict,
    16→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
    17→    shared_prefix: str,
    18→    tools_prefix: str,
    19→    *,
    20→    detect_boundary_candidates_fn,
    21→    rel_fn,
    22→    make_issue_fn,
    23→    log_fn,
    24→) -> tuple[list[Issue], int]:
    25→    """Create boundary-candidate issues, deduplicated against single-use."""
    26→    single_use_emitted = set()
    27→    for entry in single_entries:
    28→        is_size_ok = 50 <= entry["loc"] <= 200
    29→        is_colocated = lang.get_area and (
    30→            lang.get_area(rel_fn(entry["file"])) == lang.get_area(entry["sole_importer"])
    31→        )
    32→        if not is_size_ok and not is_colocated:
    33→            single_use_emitted.add(rel_fn(entry["file"]))
    34→
    35→    results: list[Issue] = []
    36→    deduped = 0
    37→    boundary_entries, total_shared = detect_boundary_candidates_fn(
    38→        path,
    39→        graph,
    40→        shared_prefix=shared_prefix,
    41→        tools_prefix=tools_prefix,
    42→        skip_basenames={"index.ts", "index.tsx"},
    43→    )
    44→    for entry in boundary_entries:
    45→        if rel_fn(entry["file"]) in single_use_emitted:
    46→            deduped += 1
    47→            continue
    48→        results.append(
    49→            make_issue_fn(
    50→                "coupling",
    51→                entry["file"],
    52→                f"boundary::{entry['sole_tool']}",
    53→                tier=3,
    54→                confidence="medium",
    55→                summary=(
    56→                    f"Boundary candidate ({entry['loc']} LOC): only used by {entry['sole_tool']} "
    57→                    f"({entry['importer_count']} importers)"
    58→                ),
    59→                detail={
    60→                    "sole_tool": entry["sole_tool"],
    61→                    "importer_count": entry["importer_count"],
    62→                    "loc": entry["loc"],
    63→                },
    64→            )
    65→        )
    66→    if deduped:
    67→        log_fn(
    68→            f"         ({deduped} boundary candidates skipped — covered by single_use)"
    69→        )
    70→    return results, total_shared
    71→
    72→
    73→def phase_coupling(
    74→    path: Path,
    75→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
    76→    *,
    77→    make_boundary_issues_fn,
    78→    build_dep_graph_fn,
    79→    detect_single_use_fn,
    80→    get_src_path_fn,
    81→    detect_coupling_violations_fn,
    82→    detect_cross_tool_imports_fn,
    83→    detect_cycles_and_orphans_fn,
    84→    detect_facades_fn,
    85→    detect_pattern_anomalies_fn,
    86→    detect_naming_inconsistencies_fn,
    87→    adjust_potential_fn,
    88→    log_fn,
    89→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
    90→    """Run the coupling phase with dependency-injected collaborators."""
    91→    results: list[Issue] = []
    92→    graph = build_dep_graph_fn(path)
    93→    lang.dep_graph = graph
    94→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
    95→
    96→    single_use_issues, single_entries, single_candidates = detect_single_use_fn(
    97→        path, graph, lang
    98→    )
    99→    results.extend(single_use_issues)
   100→
   101→    src_path = get_src_path_fn()
   102→    shared_prefix = f"{src_path}/shared/"
   103→    tools_prefix = f"{src_path}/tools/"
   104→
   105→    coupling_issues, coupling_edges = detect_coupling_violations_fn(
   106→        path, graph, lang, shared_prefix, tools_prefix
   107→    )
   108→    results.extend(coupling_issues)
   109→
   110→    boundary_issues, _ = make_boundary_issues_fn(
   111→        single_entries, path, graph, lang, shared_prefix, tools_prefix
   112→    )
   113→    results.extend(boundary_issues)
   114→
   115→    cross_tool_issues, cross_edges = detect_cross_tool_imports_fn(
   116→        path, graph, lang, tools_prefix
   117→    )
   118→    results.extend(cross_tool_issues)
   119→
   120→    cycle_orphan_issues, total_graph_files = detect_cycles_and_orphans_fn(path, graph, lang)
   121→    results.extend(cycle_orphan_issues)
   122→
   123→    results.extend(detect_facades_fn(graph, lang))
   124→
   125→    pattern_issues, total_areas = detect_pattern_anomalies_fn(path)
   126→    results.extend(pattern_issues)
   127→
   128→    naming_issues, total_dirs = detect_naming_inconsistencies_fn(path, lang)
   129→    results.extend(naming_issues)
   130→
   131→    log_fn(f"         → {len(results)} coupling/structural issues total")
   132→    potentials = {
   133→        "single_use": adjust_potential_fn(zone_map, single_candidates),
   134→        "coupling": coupling_edges + cross_edges,
   135→        "cycles": adjust_potential_fn(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   136→        "orphaned": adjust_potential_fn(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   137→        "patterns": total_areas,
   138→        "naming": total_dirs,
   139→        "facade": adjust_potential_fn(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   140→    }
   141→    return results, potentials
   142→
   143→
   144→__all__ = ["make_boundary_issues", "phase_coupling"]
   145→

   141→def update_installed_skill(interface: str) -> bool:
   142→    """Download and install the skill document for the given interface.
   143→
   144→    Returns True on success, False on failure. Prints status messages.
   145→    """
   146→    target_rel, overlay_name, dedicated = SKILL_TARGETS[interface]
   147→    target_path = get_project_root() / target_rel
   148→
   149→    print(colorize(f"Downloading skill document ({interface})...", "dim"))
   150→    try:
   151→        skill_content = _download("SKILL.md")
   152→        overlay_content = _download(f"{overlay_name}.md") if overlay_name else None
   153→    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError) as exc:
   154→        print(colorize(f"Download failed: {exc}", "red"))
   155→        return False
   156→
   157→    if "desloppify-skill-version" not in skill_content:
   158→        print(colorize("Downloaded content doesn't look like a skill document.", "red"))
   159→        return False
   160→
   161→    new_section = _build_section(skill_content, overlay_content)
   162→    if interface in _FRONTMATTER_FIRST_INTERFACES:
   163→        new_section = _ensure_frontmatter_first(new_section)
   164→
   165→    target_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   166→    if dedicated:
   167→        result = new_section
   168→    elif target_path.is_file():
   169→        existing = target_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   170→        result = _replace_section(existing, new_section)
   171→    else:
   172→        result = new_section
   173→
   174→    safe_write_text(target_path, result)
   175→
   176→    version_match = SKILL_VERSION_RE.search(new_section)
   177→    version = version_match.group(1) if version_match else "?"
   178→    print(
   179→        colorize(
   180→            f"Updated {target_rel} (v{version}, tool expects v{SKILL_VERSION})",
   181→            "green",
   182→        )
   183→    )
   184→    return True
   185→
   186→
   187→def cmd_update_skill(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   188→    """Install or update the desloppify skill document."""
   189→    interface = resolve_interface(getattr(args, "interface", None))
   190→
   191→    if not interface:
   192→        print(colorize("No installed skill document found.", "yellow"))
   193→        print()
   194→        names = ", ".join(sorted(SKILL_TARGETS))
   195→        print(f"Install with: desloppify update-skill <{names}>")
   196→        return
   197→
   198→    if interface not in SKILL_TARGETS:
   199→        names = ", ".join(sorted(SKILL_TARGETS))
   200→        print(colorize(f"Unknown interface '{interface}'.", "red"))
   201→        print(f"Available: {names}")
   202→        return
   203→
   204→    update_installed_skill(interface)
   205→

## Research Summary: `plan skip` Command Architecture

Based on my comprehensive search of the codebase, here's the complete picture of how the `plan skip` command is implemented and how attestation works:

---

### 1. **CLI Command Registration & Flag Definition**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/cli_support/parser_groups_plan_impl_sections_annotations.py` (lines 26-57)

The `plan skip` subcommand is registered with the following flags:

```python
def _add_skip_subparsers(plan_sub) -> None:
    p_skip = plan_sub.add_parser(
        "skip",
        help="Skip issues: temporary (default), --permanent (wontfix), or --false-positive",
    )
    p_skip.add_argument("patterns", nargs="+", metavar="PATTERN", ...)
    p_skip.add_argument("--reason", type=str, default=None, 
                        help="Why this is being skipped")
    p_skip.add_argument("--review-after", type=int, default=None, ...)
    p_skip.add_argument("--permanent", action="store_true", ...)
    p_skip.add_argument("--false-positive", action="store_true", ...)
    p_skip.add_argument("--note", type=str, default=None, 
                        help="Explanation (required for --permanent)")
    p_skip.add_argument("--attest", type=str, default=None,
                        help="Attestation (required for --permanent and --false-positive)")
    p_skip.add_argument("--confirm", action="store_true", default=False,
                        help="Required when skipping more than 5 items at once")
```

**Key Flags:**
- `--reason`: Optional, no validation (just stored as-is)
- `--attest`: Optional string for permanent/false_positive skips
- `--note`: Optional explanation, required for `--permanent`
- `--confirm`: Boolean flag required when bulk-skipping > 5 items
- `--permanent`: Mutually-exclusive flag
- `--false-positive`: Mutually-exclusive flag

---

### 2. **Command Handler Implementation**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/override_skip.py` (lines 91-180)

The `cmd_plan_skip()` function:

1. **Extracts CLI arguments** (lines 98-104):
   ```python
   patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   reason: str | None = getattr(args, "reason", None)
   review_after: int | None = getattr(args, "review_after", None)
   permanent: bool = getattr(args, "permanent", False)
   false_positive: bool = getattr(args, "false_positive", False)
   note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attest", None)
   ```

2. **Determines skip kind** (line 106):
   ```python
   kind = skip_kind_from_flags(permanent=permanent, false_positive=false_positive)
   ```

3. **Validates requirements** (line 107):
   ```python
   if not _validate_skip_requirements(kind=kind, attestation=attestation, note=note):
       return
   ```

4. **Bulk-skip confirmation** (lines 118-130):
   ```python
   if len(issue_ids) > _BULK_SKIP_THRESHOLD:  # threshold = 5
       if not getattr(args, "confirm", False):
           raise CommandError(
               f"Skipping {len(issue_ids)} items requires --confirm. "
               "Review the items first, or skip individually."
           )
   ```

---

### 3. **Attestation Validation Logic**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/override_skip.py` (lines 44-65)

The `_validate_skip_requirements()` function:

```python
def _validate_skip_requirements(*, kind: str, attestation: str | None, note: str | None) -> bool:
    if not skip_kind_requires_attestation(kind):
        return True
    if not validate_attestation(attestation):
        show_attestation_requirement(
            "Permanent skip" if kind == "permanent" else "False positive",
            attestation,
            ATTEST_EXAMPLE,
        )
        return False
    if skip_kind_requires_note(kind) and not note:
        print(colorize("  --permanent requires --note to explain the decision.", "yellow"), ...)
        return False
    return True
```

### 4. **Attestation Policy Functions**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/skip_policy.py`

```python
def skip_kind_requires_attestation(kind: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when the skip kind requires attestation text."""
    return kind in {"permanent", "false_positive"}

def skip_kind_requires_note(kind: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when the skip kind requires a user note."""
    return kind == "permanent"
```

**Requirements Summary:**
- **temporary**: No attestation required, no note required
- **permanent**: Attestation REQUIRED + Note REQUIRED
- **false_positive**: Attestation REQUIRED (note is optional)

### 5. **Attestation Validation Details**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/helpers/attestation.py` (lines 9-46)

```python
_REQUIRED_ATTESTATION_PHRASES = ("i have actually", "not gaming")
_ATTESTATION_KEYWORD_HINT = ("I have actually", "not gaming")

def validate_attestation(attestation: str | None) -> bool:
    return not _missing_attestation_keywords(attestation)

def _missing_attestation_keywords(attestation: str | None) -> list[str]:
    normalized = " ".join((attestation or "").strip().lower().split())
    return [
        phrase for phrase in _REQUIRED_ATTESTATION_PHRASES if phrase not in normalized
    ]
```

**Attestation Requirements:**
- Must contain BOTH "i have actually" AND "not gaming" (case-insensitive)
- Example from resolve command: `"I have actually [DESCRIBE THE CONCRETE CHANGE YOU MADE] and I am not gaming the score by resolving without fixing."`

def skip_items(
    plan: PlanModel,
    issue_ids: list[str],
    *,
    kind: str = "temporary",
    reason: str | None = None,
    note: str | None = None,
    attestation: str | None = None,
    review_after: int | None = None,
    scan_count: int = 0,
) -> int:
    """Move issue IDs to the skipped dict. Returns count skipped."""
    for fid in issue_ids:
        skipped[fid] = {
            "issue_id": fid,
            "kind": kind,
            "reason": reason,          # Stored but not validated
            "note": note,              # Required for permanent
            "attestation": attestation,  # Required for permanent/false_positive
            "created_at": now,
            "review_after": review_after,  # For temporary resurfacing
            "skipped_at_scan": scan_count,
        }
```

   183→    "queue": cmd_plan_queue,
   184→    "reset": _cmd_plan_reset,
   185→    "reorder": cmd_plan_reorder,
   186→    "describe": cmd_plan_describe,
   187→    "resolve": cmd_plan_resolve,
   188→    "note": cmd_plan_note,
   189→    "focus": cmd_plan_focus,
   190→    "skip": cmd_plan_skip,
   191→    "unskip": cmd_plan_unskip,
   192→    "reopen": cmd_plan_reopen,
   193→    "cluster": cmd_cluster_dispatch,
   194→    "triage": cmd_plan_triage,
   195→    "scan-gate": cmd_plan_scan_gate,
   196→    "commit-log": cmd_commit_log_dispatch,
   197→}
   198→
   199→
   200→def cmd_plan(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   201→    """Dispatch plan subcommand or generate markdown output."""
   202→    plan_action = getattr(args, "plan_action", None)
   203→    if plan_action is None:
   204→        _cmd_plan_generate(args)
   205→        return
   206→
   207→    handler = _PLAN_ACTION_HANDLERS.get(plan_action)
   208→    if handler is None:
   209→        print(f"Unknown plan action: {plan_action}")
   210→        return
   211→    handler(args)
   212→
   213→__all__ = ["cmd_plan", "cmd_plan_output"]
   214→

    91→def cmd_plan_skip(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:

   105→
   106→    kind = skip_kind_from_flags(permanent=permanent, false_positive=false_positive)

   301→    assert "gone" not in plan["skipped"]
   302→    assert "gone" in plan["superseded"]
   303→
   304→
   305→def test_reconcile_resurfaced():
   306→    plan = _plan_with_queue()
   307→    skip_items(plan, ["a"], kind="temporary", review_after=2, scan_count=3)
   308→    state = _state_with_issues("a")
   309→    state["scan_count"] = 5  # 3+2 = 5, should resurface
   310→
   311→    result = reconcile_plan_after_scan(plan, state)
   312→    assert "a" in result.resurfaced
   313→    assert "a" in plan["queue_order"]
   314→    assert "a" not in plan["skipped"]
   315→
   316→
   317→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   318→# Full roundtrip
   319→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   320→
   321→def test_skip_and_unskip_roundtrip():
   322→    plan = _plan_with_queue("a", "b", "c")
   323→
   324→    # Skip temporary
   325→    skip_items(plan, ["a"], kind="temporary", reason="later")
   326→    assert "a" not in plan["queue_order"]
   327→    assert plan["skipped"]["a"]["kind"] == "temporary"
   328→
   329→    # Skip permanent
   330→    skip_items(plan, ["b"], kind="permanent", note="won't fix", attestation="attest")
   331→    assert "b" not in plan["queue_order"]
   332→    assert plan["skipped"]["b"]["kind"] == "permanent"
   333→
   334→    # Skip false positive
   335→    skip_items(plan, ["c"], kind="false_positive", attestation="attest")
   336→    assert plan["queue_order"] == []
   337→    assert len(plan["skipped"]) == 3
   338→
   339→    # Unskip all — b is protected (permanent with note), c is not (fp without note)
   340→    count, need_reopen, protected = unskip_items(plan, ["a", "b", "c"])
   341→    assert count == 2  # a (temporary) + c (fp without note)
   342→    assert set(need_reopen) == {"c"}
   343→    assert protected == ["b"]
   344→    assert "a" in plan["queue_order"]
   345→    assert "b" not in plan["queue_order"]  # protected
   346→    assert "c" in plan["queue_order"]
   347→    assert "b" in plan["skipped"]  # stayed
   348→
   349→    # Force unskip to get b too
   350→    count2, need_reopen2, protected2 = unskip_items(plan, ["b"], include_protected=True)
   351→    assert count2 == 1
   352→    assert need_reopen2 == ["b"]
   353→    assert protected2 == []
   354→    assert "b" in plan["queue_order"]
   355→    assert plan["skipped"] == {}

   373→    # Override still exists (notes kept for history) but cluster cleared

1→"""Shared attestation and note validation helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import sys
     6→
     7→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     8→
     9→_REQUIRED_ATTESTATION_PHRASES = ("i have actually", "not gaming")
    10→_ATTESTATION_KEYWORD_HINT = ("I have actually", "not gaming")
    11→_MIN_NOTE_LENGTH = 50
    12→
    13→
    14→def _emit_warning(message: str) -> None:
    15→    """Write resolve preflight warnings to stderr consistently."""
    16→    print(colorize(message, "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
    17→
    18→
    19→def _missing_attestation_keywords(attestation: str | None) -> list[str]:
    20→    normalized = " ".join((attestation or "").strip().lower().split())
    21→    return [
    22→        phrase for phrase in _REQUIRED_ATTESTATION_PHRASES if phrase not in normalized
    23→    ]
    24→
    25→
    26→def validate_attestation(attestation: str | None) -> bool:
    27→    return not _missing_attestation_keywords(attestation)
    28→
    29→
    30→def show_attestation_requirement(
    31→    label: str,
    32→    attestation: str | None,
    33→    example: str,
    34→) -> None:
    35→    missing = _missing_attestation_keywords(attestation)
    36→    if not attestation:
    37→        _emit_warning(f"{label} requires --attest.")
    38→    elif missing:
    39→        missing_str = ", ".join(f"'{keyword}'" for keyword in missing)
    40→        _emit_warning(
    41→            f"{label} attestation is missing required keyword(s): {missing_str}."
    42→        )
    43→    _emit_warning(
    44→        f"Required keywords: '{_ATTESTATION_KEYWORD_HINT[0]}' and '{_ATTESTATION_KEYWORD_HINT[1]}'."
    45→    )
    46→    print(colorize(f'Example: --attest "{example}"', "dim"), file=sys.stderr)
    47→
    48→
    49→def validate_note_length(note: str | None) -> bool:
    50→    """Return True if the note meets the minimum length requirement."""
    51→    return note is not None and len(note.strip()) >= _MIN_NOTE_LENGTH
    52→
    53→
    54→def show_note_length_requirement(note: str | None) -> None:
    55→    """Emit a warning about minimum note length."""
    56→    current = len((note or "").strip())
    57→    _emit_warning(
    58→        f"Note must be at least {_MIN_NOTE_LENGTH} characters (got {current}). "
    59→        f"Describe what you actually did."
    60→    )
    61→
    62→
    63→__all__ = [
    64→    "_MIN_NOTE_LENGTH",
    65→    "show_attestation_requirement",
    66→    "show_note_length_requirement",
    67→    "validate_attestation",
    68→    "validate_note_length",
    69→]

    31→  desloppify plan                       # full prioritized markdown
    32→  desloppify plan queue                 # compact table of all items
    33→  desloppify plan cluster create ...    # group related issues
    34→  desloppify plan focus <cluster>       # narrow scope
    35→  desloppify next                       # work on the next item
    36→  desloppify plan resolve <id> --attest .. # mark as fixed
    37→
    38→patterns (used by reorder, skip, resolve, describe, note, etc.):
    39→  Patterns match issues by detector, file, ID prefix, glob, or name.
    40→  Cluster names also work as patterns — they expand to all member IDs.

    21→
    22→def skip_kind_from_flags(*, permanent: bool, false_positive: bool) -> str:
    23→    """Map CLI flags to a canonical skip kind."""
    24→    if false_positive:
    25→        return "false_positive"
    26→    if permanent:
    27→        return "permanent"
    28→    return "temporary"
    29→
    30→
    31→def skip_kind_requires_attestation(kind: str) -> bool:
    32→    """Return True when the skip kind requires attestation text."""
    33→    return kind in {"permanent", "false_positive"}
    34→
    35→
    36→def skip_kind_requires_note(kind: str) -> bool:
    37→    """Return True when the skip kind requires a user note."""
    38→    return kind == "permanent"
    39→
    40→
    41→def skip_kind_state_status(kind: str) -> str | None:
    42→    """Return corresponding state status, if any."""
    43→    if kind == "permanent":
    44→        return "wontfix"
    45→    if kind == "false_positive":
    46→        return "false_positive"
    47→    return None
    48→
    49→
    50→def skip_kind_needs_state_reopen(kind: str) -> bool:
    51→    """Return True when unskip should reopen state-layer status."""
    52→    return kind in {"permanent", "false_positive"}
    53→

    22→def detail_dict(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    23→    """Return issue detail as a dict; tolerate legacy/non-dict payloads."""
    24→    detail = item.get("detail")
    25→    return detail if isinstance(detail, dict) else {}
    26→
    27→
    28→def status_matches(item_status: str, status_filter: str) -> bool:
    29→    return status_filter == "all" or item_status == status_filter
    30→
    31→
    32→def is_subjective_issue(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    33→    detector = item.get("detector")
    34→    return detector in {"subjective_assessment", "holistic_review"}
    35→
    36→
    37→def is_review_issue(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    38→    return item.get("detector") == "review"
    39→
    40→
    41→def is_subjective_queue_item(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    42→    """True for subjective work items, including collapsed subjective clusters."""
    43→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
    44→        return True
    45→    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
    46→        members = item.get("members", [])
    47→        return bool(members) and all(
    48→            m.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension" for m in members
    49→        )
    50→    return False
    51→
    52→
    53→def review_issue_weight(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any]) -> float:
    54→    """Return review issue weight aligned with issues list ordering."""
    55→    confidence = str(item.get("confidence", "low")).lower()
    56→    weight_by_confidence = {
    57→        "high": 1.0,
    58→        "medium": 0.7,
    59→        "low": 0.3,
    60→    }
    61→    weight = weight_by_confidence.get(confidence, 0.3)
    62→    if detail_dict(item).get("holistic"):
    63→        weight *= 10.0
    64→    return float(weight)
    65→
    66→
    67→def scope_matches(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any], scope: str | None) -> bool:
    68→    """Apply show-style pattern matching against a queue item."""
    69→    if not scope:
    70→        return True
    71→
    72→    item_id = item.get("id", "")
    73→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
    74→    filepath = item.get("file", "")
    75→    summary = item.get("summary", "")
    76→    dimension = detail_dict(item).get("dimension_name", "")
    77→    kind = item.get("kind", "")
    78→
    79→    if "*" in scope:
    80→        return any(
    81→            fnmatch(candidate, scope)
    82→            for candidate in (item_id, filepath, detector, dimension, summary)
    83→        )
    84→
    85→    if "::" in scope:
    86→        return item_id.startswith(scope)
    87→
    88→    lowered = scope.lower()
    89→    if kind == "subjective_dimension":
    90→        return (
    91→            lowered in item_id.lower()
    92→            or lowered in dimension.lower()
    93→            or lowered in summary.lower()
    94→        )
    95→
    96→    # Hash suffix: 8+ hex chars matches the tail segment of a issue ID.
    97→    if len(lowered) >= 8 and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]+", lowered):
    98→        return item_id.lower().endswith("::" + lowered)

     8→from desloppify.engine._plan.skip_policy import skip_kind_needs_state_reopen
     9→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import utc_now
    10→
    11→
    12→def skip_items(
    13→    plan: PlanModel,
    14→    issue_ids: list[str],
    15→    *,
    16→    kind: str = "temporary",
    17→    reason: str | None = None,
    18→    note: str | None = None,
    19→    attestation: str | None = None,
    20→    review_after: int | None = None,
    21→    scan_count: int = 0,
    22→) -> int:
    23→    """Move issue IDs to the skipped dict. Returns count skipped."""
    24→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    25→    now = utc_now()
    26→    count = 0
    27→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
    28→    skip_set = set(issue_ids)
    29→    prune_promoted_ids(plan, skip_set)
    30→    for fid in issue_ids:
    31→        _remove_id_from_lists(plan, fid)
    32→        skipped[fid] = {
    33→            "issue_id": fid,
    34→            "kind": kind,
    35→            "reason": reason,
    36→            "note": note,
    37→            "attestation": attestation,
    38→            "created_at": now,
    39→            "review_after": review_after,
    40→            "skipped_at_scan": scan_count,
    41→        }
    42→        count += 1
    43→    return count
    44→
    45→
    46→def _is_protected_skip(entry: SkipEntry) -> bool:
    47→    """A skip is protected if it was permanent/false_positive AND has a note.
    48→
    49→    Protected skips represent deliberate human judgment and should not be
    50→    silently undone by bulk unskip operations.
    51→    """
    52→    kind = str(entry.get("kind", ""))
    53→    has_note = bool(entry.get("note", ""))
    54→    return kind in ("permanent", "false_positive") and has_note
    55→
    56→
    57→def unskip_items(
    58→    plan: PlanModel,
    59→    issue_ids: list[str],
    60→    *,
    61→    include_protected: bool = False,
    62→) -> tuple[int, list[str], list[str]]:
    63→    """Bring issue IDs back from skipped to the end of queue_order.
    64→
    65→    Returns ``(count_unskipped, permanent_ids_needing_state_reopen, protected_ids_kept)``
    66→    where the second list contains IDs that were permanent or false_positive
    67→    and need their state-layer status reopened by the caller, and the third
    68→    list contains protected IDs that were NOT unskipped (unless
    69→    ``include_protected=True``).
    70→    """
    71→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    72→    count = 0
    73→    need_reopen: list[str] = []
    74→    protected_kept: list[str] = []
    75→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
    76→    for fid in issue_ids:
    77→        entry = skipped.get(fid)
    78→        if entry is None:
    79→            continue
    80→        if not include_protected and _is_protected_skip(entry):
    81→            protected_kept.append(fid)
    82→            continue
    83→        skipped.pop(fid)
    84→        if skip_kind_needs_state_reopen(str(entry.get("kind", ""))):
    85→            need_reopen.append(fid)
    86→        if fid not in plan["queue_order"]:
    87→            plan["queue_order"].append(fid)
    88→        count += 1
    89→    return count, need_reopen, protected_kept
    90→
    91→
    92→def resurface_stale_skips(
    93→    plan: PlanModel, current_scan_count: int
    94→) -> list[str]:
    95→    """Move temporary skips past their review_after threshold back to queue.
    96→
    97→    Returns list of resurfaced issue IDs.
    98→    """
    99→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   100→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   101→    resurfaced: list[str] = []
   102→    for fid in list(skipped):
   103→        entry = skipped[fid]
   104→        if entry.get("kind") != "temporary":
   105→            continue
   106→        review_after = entry.get("review_after")
   107→        if review_after is None:
   108→            continue
   109→        skipped_at = entry.get("skipped_at_scan", 0)
   110→        if current_scan_count >= skipped_at + review_after:
   111→            skipped.pop(fid)
   112→            if fid not in plan["queue_order"]:
   113→                plan["queue_order"].append(fid)
   114→            resurfaced.append(fid)
   115→    return resurfaced
   116→
   117→
   118→__all__ = ["resurface_stale_skips", "skip_items", "unskip_items"]
   119→
```

The `plan skip` subcommand is registered with the following flags:

```python
def _add_skip_subparsers(plan_sub) -> None:
    p_skip = plan_sub.add_parser(
        "skip",
        help="Skip issues: temporary (default), --permanent (wontfix), or --false-positive",
    )
    p_skip.add_argument("patterns", nargs="+", metavar="PATTERN", ...)
    p_skip.add_argument("--reason", type=str, default=None, 
                        help="Why this is being skipped")
    p_skip.add_argument("--review-after", type=int, default=None, ...)
    p_skip.add_argument("--permanent", action="store_true", ...)
    p_skip.add_argument("--false-positive", action="store_true", ...)
    p_skip.add_argument("--note", type=str, default=None, 
                        help="Explanation (required for --permanent)")
    p_skip.add_argument("--attest", type=str, default=None,
                        help="Attestation (required for --permanent and --false-positive)")
    p_skip.add_argument("--confirm", action="store_true", default=False,
                        help="Required when skipping more than 5 items at once")
```

**Key Flags:**
- `--reason`: Optional, no validation (just stored as-is)
- `--attest`: Optional string for permanent/false_positive skips
- `--note`: Optional explanation, required for `--permanent`
- `--confirm`: Boolean flag required when bulk-skipping > 5 items
- `--permanent`: Mutually-exclusive flag
- `--false-positive`: Mutually-exclusive flag

def _validate_skip_requirements(*, kind: str, attestation: str | None, note: str | None) -> bool:

        return True
    if not validate_attestation(attestation):
        show_attestation_requirement(

### 4. **Attestation Policy Functions**

```python
def skip_kind_requires_attestation(kind: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when the skip kind requires attestation text."""
    return kind in {"permanent", "false_positive"}

def skip_kind_requires_note(kind: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when the skip kind requires a user note."""
    return kind == "permanent"
```

**Requirements Summary:**
- **temporary**: No attestation required, no note required
- **permanent**: Attestation REQUIRED + Note REQUIRED
- **false_positive**: Attestation REQUIRED (note is optional)

### 5. **Attestation Validation Details**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/helpers/attestation.py` (lines 9-46)

```python
_REQUIRED_ATTESTATION_PHRASES = ("i have actually", "not gaming")
_ATTESTATION_KEYWORD_HINT = ("I have actually", "not gaming")

def validate_attestation(attestation: str | None) -> bool:
    return not _missing_attestation_keywords(attestation)

def _missing_attestation_keywords(attestation: str | None) -> list[str]:
    normalized = " ".join((attestation or "").strip().lower().split())
    return [
        phrase for phrase in _REQUIRED_ATTESTATION_PHRASES if phrase not in normalized
    ]
```

**Attestation Requirements:**
- Must contain BOTH "i have actually" AND "not gaming" (case-insensitive)
- Example from resolve command: `"I have actually [DESCRIBE THE CONCRETE CHANGE YOU MADE] and I am not gaming the score by resolving without fixing."`

def skip_items(
    plan: PlanModel,

    *,
    kind: str = "temporary",
    reason: str | None = None,
    note: str | None = None,
    attestation: str | None = None,
    review_after: int | None = None,
    scan_count: int = 0,
) -> int:
    """Move issue IDs to the skipped dict. Returns count skipped."""

        skipped[fid] = {
            "issue_id": fid,
            "kind": kind,
            "reason": reason,          # Stored but not validated
            "note": note,              # Required for permanent
            "attestation": attestation,  # Required for permanent/false_positive
            "created_at": now,
            "review_after": review_after,  # For temporary resurfacing
            "skipped_at_scan": scan_count,
        }
```

   125→        )
   126→        if not getattr(args, "confirm", False):
   127→            raise CommandError(

   129→                "Review the items first, or skip individually."
   130→            )

   132→    state_data = _apply_state_skip_resolution(
   133→        kind=kind,
   134→        state_file=state_file,
   135→        issue_ids=issue_ids,
   136→        note=note,
   137→        attestation=attestation,
   138→    )
   139→
   140→    scan_count = state.get("scan_count", 0)
   141→    count = skip_items(
   142→        plan,
   143→        issue_ids,
   144→        kind=kind,
   145→        reason=reason,
   146→        note=note,
   147→        attestation=attestation,
   148→        review_after=review_after,
   149→        scan_count=scan_count,
   150→    )
   151→
   152→    append_log_entry(
   153→        plan,
   154→        "skip",
   155→        issue_ids=issue_ids,
   156→        actor="user",
   157→        note=note,
   158→        detail={"kind": kind, "reason": reason},
   159→    )
   160→    if state_data is not None:
   161→        save_plan_state_transactional(
   162→            plan=plan,
   163→            plan_path=plan_file,
   164→            state_data=state_data,
   165→            state_path_value=state_file,
   166→        )
   167→    else:
   168→        save_plan(plan, plan_file)
   169→
   170→    print(colorize(f"  {SKIP_KIND_LABELS[kind]} {count} item(s).", "green"))
   171→    if review_after:
   172→        print(colorize(f"  Will re-surface after {review_after} scan(s).", "dim"))
   173→    print_user_message(
   174→        "Hey — if skipping was the right call, just continue with"
   175→        " what you were doing. If you think a broader re-triage is"

   177→        " plan --help` to see all available plan tools. Otherwise"
   178→        " no need to reply, just keep going."
   179→    )
   180→
   181→
   182→def cmd_plan_unskip(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   183→    """Unskip issues — bring back to queue."""
   184→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   185→    state = runtime.state
   186→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   187→        return
   188→
   189→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   190→
   191→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   192→    plan_file = _plan_file_for_state(state_file)
   193→    plan = load_plan(plan_file)
   194→    issue_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, patterns, plan=plan, status_filter="all")
   195→    if not issue_ids:
   196→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found.", "yellow"))
   197→        return
   198→
   199→    include_protected = bool(getattr(args, "force", False))
   200→    count, need_reopen, protected_kept = unskip_items(
   201→        plan,
   202→        issue_ids,
   203→        include_protected=include_protected,
   204→    )
   205→    unskipped_ids = [fid for fid in issue_ids if fid not in protected_kept]
   206→    append_log_entry(
   207→        plan,
   208→        "unskip",
   209→        issue_ids=unskipped_ids,
   210→        actor="user",
   211→        detail={"need_reopen": need_reopen},
   212→    )
   213→
   214→    reopened: list[str] = []
   215→    if need_reopen:
   216→        state_data = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
   217→        for fid in need_reopen:
   218→            reopened.extend(state_mod.resolve_issues(state_data, fid, "open"))
   219→        save_plan_state_transactional(
   220→            plan=plan,
   221→            plan_path=plan_file,
   222→            state_data=state_data,
   223→            state_path_value=state_file,
   224→        )
   225→        print(colorize(f"  Reopened {len(reopened)} issue(s) in state.", "dim"))
   226→    else:
   227→        save_plan(plan, plan_file)
   228→
   229→    print(colorize(f"  Unskipped {count} item(s) — back in queue.", "green"))
   230→    if protected_kept:
   231→        print(
   232→            colorize(
   233→                f"  Kept {len(protected_kept)} protected skip(s) "
   234→                f"(permanent/false_positive with notes). Use --force to override.",
   235→                "yellow",
   236→            )
   237→        )
   238→
   239→
   240→__all__ = [
   241→    "_apply_state_skip_resolution",
   242→    "_validate_skip_requirements",
   243→    "cmd_plan_skip",
   244→    "cmd_plan_unskip",
   245→]

> AGENT

The auto-generated attestation won't pass `validate_attestation()` since it requires "not gaming" and our text says "not deferring." But the attestation is only checked for permanent/false_positive skips (via `_validate_skip_requirements`), not temporary ones. The `--confirm` auto-generates attestation for *storage* purposes — it won't hit the validation check for temporary skips.

Let me verify this by tracing the flow: `--confirm` is typically used without `--permanent`/`--false_positive`, so `kind = "temporary"`, and `skip_kind_requires_attestation("temporary")` returns `False`, so `_validate_skip_requirements` returns `True` without checking the attestation content. The attestation just gets stored in the skip record.

That's the right behavior — the attestation is a record of reflection, not a gating check for temporary skips. Let me run the tests to make sure.

All passing. Here's the logic now:

**Temporary skip + `--confirm`**: requires `--reason` + `--attest "I have actually reflected and I am not deferring this for lazy reasons."` (deferral-specific phrases)

OK, now I have the full picture. Two bugs:

1. **`resolve_ids_from_patterns` doesn't glob-match against plan IDs** — `plan_ids` check is literal only, so `subjective::*` fails
2. **`resolve_ids_from_patterns` doesn't match against skipped IDs for glob/prefix patterns** — even without globs, if someone passes a prefix pattern, it won't match skipped items

But there's actually a simpler conceptual issue: **`plan skip --permanent` on an already-skipped ID should just promote its kind**. It shouldn't need to go through resolve → skip_items (which overwrites the entry). The operation is "reclassify this skip," not "skip this open issue."

Let me fix `_resolve.py` to glob-match against plan IDs, which is the minimal fix that unblocks the use case.

> AGENT

4814 passed. Here's the root cause and fix:

**Root cause:** `resolve_ids_from_patterns` checked plan IDs (including skipped) with literal equality only. Glob patterns like `subjective::*` and prefix patterns like `subjective::a` only matched against the active work queue, not against skipped/clustered plan IDs. So `plan skip --permanent subjective::*` would find zero matches for plan-only IDs that were already in temporary skip.

**Fix:** Added a glob/prefix match step against `plan_ids` (which includes skipped, queued, and clustered IDs) before falling through to the queue-only search. Now `subjective::*` correctly resolves all 20 temp-skipped subjective IDs, so `plan skip --permanent` can promote them directly.

    12→def _append_unique(issue_id: str, seen: set[str], result: list[str]) -> None:

    14→        return
    15→    seen.add(issue_id)
    16→    result.append(issue_id)

    19→def _collect_plan_ids(plan: PlanModel | None) -> set[str]:
    20→    plan_ids: set[str] = set()
    21→    if plan is None:
    22→        return plan_ids
    23→    plan_ids.update(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    24→    plan_ids.update(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
    25→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    26→        plan_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    27→    return plan_ids
    28→
    29→
    30→def _collect_queue_ids(state: StateModel, plan: PlanModel | None) -> set[str]:
    31→    """Return IDs currently visible in the active queue (including synthetic IDs)."""
    32→    queue = build_work_queue(
    33→        state,
    34→        options=QueueBuildOptions(
    35→            count=None,
    36→            plan=plan,
    37→        ),
    38→    )
    39→    out: set[str] = set()
    40→    for item in queue.get("items", []):
    41→        issue_id = item.get("id")
    42→        if isinstance(issue_id, str) and issue_id:
    43→            out.add(issue_id)
    44→    return out
    45→
    46→
    47→def _queue_pattern_matches(queue_ids: set[str], pattern: str) -> list[str]:
    48→    """Match a plan pattern against queue IDs (supports literals + globs)."""
    49→    matches: list[str] = []
    50→    for issue_id in queue_ids:
    51→        if issue_id == pattern:
    52→            matches.append(issue_id)
    53→            continue
    54→        if "*" in pattern and fnmatch.fnmatch(issue_id, pattern):
    55→            matches.append(issue_id)
    56→            continue
    57→        if issue_id.startswith(pattern):
    58→            matches.append(issue_id)
    59→    return sorted(set(matches))
    60→
    61→
    62→def resolve_ids_from_patterns(
    63→    state: StateModel,
    64→    patterns: list[str],
    65→    *,
    66→    plan: PlanModel | None = None,
    67→    status_filter: str = "open",
    68→) -> list[str]:
    69→    """Resolve one or more patterns to a deduplicated list of issue IDs.
    70→
    71→    When *plan* is provided, literal IDs that exist only in the plan

    86→        if pattern in plan_ids:

Two other literal-only spots exist, both for **cluster name matching**:

1. **`_resolve.py:103`** — `pattern in plan.get("clusters", {})` — if you pass `cluster-*` it won't glob-match cluster names.

2. **`override_resolve_helpers.py:16`** — `check_cluster_guard` does `if pattern in clusters:` — same literal-only check.

However, these are a **different risk profile** than the `subjective::*` bug. Cluster names are short, user-defined labels like `"naming-cleanup"` or `"cluster-a"`. Users type the exact name they chose. Nobody would realistically glob-match cluster names — you'd have to have created multiple clusters with a shared prefix and then want to operate on all of them at once, which is an unusual workflow.

The `subjective::*` bug was nasty because synthetic IDs are system-generated, long, and prefixed — exactly the pattern where users naturally reach for globs. Cluster names don't have that property.

`resolve_synthetic_ids` in `override_resolve_helpers.py:74` is also literal-only, but it's just a **classification** function (routing synthetic vs real patterns), not a resolution function. It checks `startswith("triage::")` etc. to decide which code path handles them. It doesn't need glob support.

**Verdict**: The fix you already have in `resolve_ids_from_patterns` was the only spot where the literal-only matching was actually causing real failures. The cluster name spots are technically literal-only but don't pose a practical risk.

## Work Queue Drainage Flow - Complete Research Report

Based on my thorough exploration of the desloppify codebase, here's the complete flow for what happens when the work queue is cleared/drained:

### 1. **Queue Drainage Triggers Rescan & Subjective Analysis Cycle**

The flow is triggered by the **post-scan plan reconciliation** in `reconcile_plan_post_scan()` (called from `merge_scan_results()` at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/scan/workflow.py:424`).

**Key insight:** The queue lifecycle is divided into two **phases**:
- **Objective phase**: Mechanical detectors (fixes, issues, refactoring) 
- **Endgame/Subjective phase**: Subjective dimensions, triage, workflow checkpoints

Once all objective work is drained from the queue, the system automatically:
1. Injects subjective dimension reviews for initial assessment
2. Runs triage workflow stages (observe, reflect, organize, enrich, sense-check, commit)
3. Injects communication checkpoints and plan-creation workflows

---

### 2. **`_clear_plan_start_scores_if_queue_empty()` - The Queue Drainage Gate**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/scan/plan_reconcile.py:129-153`

This function:

```python
def _clear_plan_start_scores_if_queue_empty(state, plan) -> bool:
    """Clear plan-start score snapshot once the queue is fully drained."""
```

**What it gates:**
- Determines when to **"unfreeze" the scores** — moving from FROZEN display mode to LIVE mode
- Uses `score_display_mode(breakdown, frozen_strict)` to check if queue is truly empty
- When queue is drained: stashes old scores in `state["_plan_start_scores_for_reveal"]` and clears `plan["plan_start_scores"]`

**Return value:** `True` if it cleared the scores (queue was empty), `False` if queue still has work

---

### 3. **`sync_communicate_score_needed()` & `sync_create_plan_needed()` - Workflow Gates**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/sync_workflow.py:70-149`

#### `sync_communicate_score_needed(plan, state, policy=None)` (lines 126-149)
- **Triggers when:** All initial subjective reviews are complete (no unscored dimensions) OR scores were just imported
- **Effect:** Injects `workflow::communicate-score` queue item to show final scores
- **Guard:** Only if no checkpoint or communicate-score already present

#### `sync_create_plan_needed(plan, state, policy=None)` (lines 70-99)
- **Triggers when:**
  1. No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain ✓
  2. At least one objective issue exists ✓
  3. No triage stages pending ✓
  4. `workflow::create-plan` not already in queue
- **Effect:** Injects `workflow::create-plan` queue item to rebuild the prioritized plan
- **Guard:** Blocked by `has_objective_backlog()` check — defers until objective work is drained

**Key concept:** These workflow items don't appear until endgame conditions are met.

---

### 4. **`score_display_mode()` - Single Source of Truth for Queue Emptiness**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/helpers/queue_progress.py:75-93`

```python
def score_display_mode(breakdown: QueueBreakdown | None, 
                       plan_start_strict: float | None) -> ScoreDisplayMode:
```

**Returns three modes:**

| Mode | Condition | Display |
|------|-----------|---------|
| `FROZEN` | `plan_start_strict is not None` AND `breakdown.objective_actionable > 0` | Show frozen plan-start score + progress bar |
| `PHASE_TRANSITION` | Queue has subjective/workflow items but NO objective items | Show live scores + transition banner |
| `LIVE` | `plan_start_strict is None` OR queue is completely empty | Show normal live scores |

**Key metric:** `breakdown.objective_actionable` = `queue_total - subjective - workflow`
- This is the count used to decide frozen vs live display
- Does NOT include endgame-only items (subjective dimensions, workflow stages)

### 5. **`reconcile_plan_post_scan()` - Complete Queue Drainage Choreography**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/scan/plan_reconcile.py:309-360`

Called after every scan merge. Orchestrates these sync operations **in order**:

**Critical:** Each sync result is logged via `append_log_entry()` so the plan audit trail tracks when each workflow step was injected.

### 7. **Lifecycle Filtering: Endgame-Only Item Visibility**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/lifecycle.py:56-76`

```

**Rules:**
- If unscored dimensions exist → **show only unscored items** (block everything else)
- If triage stages exist + objective work remains → **hide triage** (but show objective)
- If no objective items remain → **show everything** (subjective, workflow, triage)

**Effect:** Subjective/triage items marked with `_is_endgame_only()` are filtered based on `_has_objective_items()` check.

**Flow:**
1. `_clear_plan_start_scores_if_queue_empty()` stashes old scores in state: `_plan_start_scores_for_reveal`
2. After `merge_scan_results()` completes, `show_score_delta()` calls `_show_score_reveal()`

**Computed once per operation** and passed to all sync functions. Provides unified answers:
- `policy.has_objective_backlog` — used to defer triage, block stale dimension injection
- `policy.unscored_ids` — gates when to inject communicate-score
- `policy.stale_ids` — evicts subjective reviews when objective work remains

### 10. **NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS - What Counts as "Work"**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/subjective_policy.py:19-22`

    "review", "concerns", "subjective_review", "subjective_assessment",
})
```

**Everything else is objective** — mechanical fixes, linting, structural issues, etc.

The queue is only considered "drained" when objective items are gone. Subjective/workflow items can remain.

---

### 11. **Constants: The Workflow Item IDs**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/constants.py:22-26`

```python
WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID = "workflow::create-plan"
WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID = "workflow::score-checkpoint"
WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID = "workflow::communicate-score"
WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID = "workflow::import-scores"
```

**Queue lifecycle order:**
1. Initial reviews → `score-checkpoint` (all unscored done)
2. Reviews complete → `communicate-score` (show scores)
3. Ready for prioritization → `create-plan` (when objective work exists)
4. Triage workflow (optional, deferred if objective work remains)

---

### Summary

The **queue drainage flow** is a sophisticated lifecycle system:

1. **Cycle starts:** `_seed_plan_start_scores()` freezes scores, marks plan as mid-cycle
2. **User works:** `apply_lifecycle_filter()` hides endgame items while objective work exists
3. **Objective drained:** Subjective items + workflow stages become visible
4. **Reviews complete:** `sync_communicate_score_needed()` injects communication checkpoint
5. **Plan rebuild:** `sync_create_plan_needed()` prepares final prioritized plan
6. **Cycle ends:** `_clear_plan_start_scores_if_queue_empty()` clears frozen scores, triggers reveal
7. **Scores updated:** `show_score_reveal()` shows before/after delta

The key insight: **`score_display_mode()` is the single source of truth** for determining when the queue is truly drained. All gating logic flows from `breakdown.objective_actionable > 0`.

    64→
    65→def is_triage_stale(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> bool:
    66→    """Side-effect-free check: is triage needed?
    67→
    68→    Returns True when genuinely *new* review issues appeared since the
    69→    last triage.  Triage stage IDs being in the queue alone is not
    70→    sufficient — the new issues that triggered injection may have been
    71→    resolved since then.
    72→
    73→    When issues are merely resolved (current IDs are a subset of
    74→    previously triaged IDs), triage is NOT stale — the user is working
    75→    through the plan.
    76→    """
    77→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    78→    return stale_policy_mod.is_triage_stale(plan, state)
    79→
    80→
    81→def compute_new_issue_ids(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> set[str]:
    82→    """Return the set of open review/concerns issue IDs added since last triage.
    83→
    84→    Returns an empty set when no prior triage has recorded ``triaged_ids``.
    85→    """
    86→    return stale_policy_mod.compute_new_issue_ids(plan, state)
    87→
    88→
    89→def sync_triage_needed(
    90→    plan: PlanModel,
    91→    state: StateModel,
    92→    *,
    93→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
    94→) -> QueueSyncResult:
    95→    """Append triage stage IDs to back of queue when review issues change.
    96→
    97→    Only injects stages not already confirmed in ``epic_triage_meta``.
    98→
    99→    **Mid-cycle guard**: when the objective backlog still has work, triage
   100→    stages are NOT injected.  Instead, ``epic_triage_meta["triage_recommended"]``
   101→    is set so the UI can show a non-blocking banner.  Stages are injected
   102→    once the objective backlog drains (or on manual ``plan triage``).
   103→
   104→    When stages are already present but all new issues have been resolved
   105→    since injection, auto-prunes the stale stages and updates the hash.
   106→
   107→    When issues are *resolved* (current IDs are a subset of previously
   108→    triaged IDs), the snapshot hash is updated silently — no re-triage
   109→    is needed since the user is working through the plan.
   110→    """
   111→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   112→    result = QueueSyncResult()
   113→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   114→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   115→    confirmed = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   116→
   117→    # Check if any triage stage is already in queue
   118→    already_present = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
   119→
   120→    current_hash = stale_policy_mod.review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   121→    last_hash = meta.get("issue_snapshot_hash", "")
   122→
   123→    if already_present:
   124→        # Stages present — check if the reason for injection still applies.
   125→        # Only auto-prune when triage was completed before (hash exists),
   126→        # all new issues have been resolved, and no triage work is in
   127→        # progress.  This avoids pruning the initial triage or a
   128→        # user-started triage session.
   129→        if last_hash and not confirmed:
   130→            new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   131→
   132→            if not new_since_triage:
   133→                # No new issues remain — prune stale stages
   134→                _prune_all_triage_stages(order)
   135→                if current_hash:
   136→                    meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   137→                    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   138→                result.pruned = list(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS)
   139→        return result
   140→
   141→    # Backfill: partial triage was done (stages confirmed with
   142→    # confirmed_at) but triage was never fully completed — remaining
   143→    # stages were skipped or removed from the queue.  Record current
   144→    # review IDs as triaged so they don't re-trigger injection on the
   145→    # next cycle.
   146→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   147→    has_completed_stage = any(
   148→        isinstance(v, dict) and v.get("confirmed_at")
   149→        for v in stages.values()
   150→    )
   151→    if has_completed_stage and not meta.get("triaged_ids") and not last_hash:
   152→        current_review = sorted(stale_policy_mod.open_review_ids(state))
   153→        if current_review:
   154→            meta["triaged_ids"] = current_review
   155→            meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   156→            plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   157→
   158→    if current_hash and current_hash != last_hash:
   159→        # Distinguish "new issues appeared" from "issues were resolved".
   160→        # Only re-triage when genuinely new issues exist.
   161→        new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   162→
   163→        if new_since_triage:
   164→            # Mid-cycle guard: defer injection while objective work remains.
   165→            if is_mid_cycle(plan) and has_objective_backlog(state, policy):
   166→                meta["triage_recommended"] = True
   167→                plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   168→                result.deferred = True
   169→            else:
   170→                # Inject: either pre-cycle, end-of-cycle, or no objective work
   171→                meta.pop("triage_recommended", None)
   172→                plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   173→                injected = _inject_pending_triage_stages(
   174→                    order,
   175→                    confirmed,
   176→                    skipped=plan.get("skipped", {}),
   177→                )
   178→                result.injected = injected
   179→        else:
   180→            # Only resolved issues changed the hash — update silently.
   181→            # Also clear triage_recommended: the issues that triggered the
   182→            # recommendation have been resolved, so it's no longer relevant.
   183→            meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   184→            meta.pop("triage_recommended", None)
   185→            plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   186→
   187→    return result
   188→
   189→
   190→__all__ = [
   191→    "compute_new_issue_ids",
   192→    "is_triage_stale",
   193→    "sync_triage_needed",
   194→]
   195→

   182→def triage_phase_banner(plan: PlanModel, state: dict | None = None) -> str:
   183→    """Return a banner string describing triage status.
   184→
   185→    Handles three states:
   186→    - Triage stages in queue + objective work → TRIAGE PENDING
   187→    - Triage stages in queue + no objective work → TRIAGE MODE (active)
   188→    - No triage stages but ``triage_recommended`` set → soft recommendation
   189→    """
   190→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   191→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   192→    has_triage = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
   193→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   194→
   195→    if not has_triage:
   196→        # No stages in queue — check for deferred recommendation
   197→        if meta.get("triage_recommended"):
   198→            return (
   199→                "TRIAGE RECOMMENDED — review issues changed since last triage. "
   200→                "Run: desloppify plan triage"
   201→            )
   202→        return ""
   203→
   204→    if state and _has_objective_backlog(state, None):
   205→        return (
   206→            "TRIAGE PENDING — queued and will activate after objective work "
   207→            "is complete."
   208→        )
   209→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   210→    completed = [s for s in ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "enrich", "sense-check") if s in stages]
   211→    if completed:
   212→        return (
   213→            f"TRIAGE MODE ({len(completed)}/5 stages complete) — "
   214→            "complete all stages to exit. Run: desloppify plan triage"
   215→        )
   216→    return (
   217→        "TRIAGE MODE — review issues need analysis before fixing. "
   218→        "Run: desloppify plan triage"
   219→    )
   220→
   221→

    34→    return bool(
    35→        plan.get("queue_order")
    36→        or plan.get("overrides")
    37→        or plan.get("clusters")
    38→        or plan.get("skipped")
    39→    )
