   752→   752→+def _low_score_dimensions(assessments: dict[str, float]) -> set[str]:
   753→   753→+    """Return assessed dimensions requiring explicit defect issues."""
   754→   754→+    return {
   755→   755→+        dim
   756→   756→+        for dim, score in assessments.items()
   757→   757→+        if score < LOW_SCORE_ISSUE_THRESHOLD
   758→   758→+    }
   759→   759→+
   760→   760→+
   761→   761→+def _enforce_low_score_issues(
   762→   762→+    *,
   763→   763→+    assessments: dict[str, float],
   764→   764→+    issues: list[NormalizedBatchIssue],
   765→   765→+) -> None:
   766→   766→+    """Fail closed when low scores do not report explicit issues."""
   767→   767→+    required_dims = _low_score_dimensions(assessments)
   768→   768→+    if not required_dims:
   769→   769→+        return
   770→   770→+    issue_dims = {
   771→   771→+        issue.dimension.strip() for issue in issues
   772→   772→+    }
   773→   773→+    missing = sorted(dim for dim in required_dims if dim not in issue_dims)
   774→   774→+    if not missing:
   775→   775→+        return
   776→   776→+    joined = ", ".join(missing)
   777→   777→+    raise ValueError(
   778→   778→+        "low-score dimensions must include at least one explicit issue: "
   779→   779→+        f"{joined} (threshold {LOW_SCORE_ISSUE_THRESHOLD:.1f})"
   780→   780→+    )

   783→   783→+def _compute_batch_quality(
   784→   784→+    assessments: dict[str, float],

   787→   787→+    high_score_missing_issue_note: float,
   788→   788→+) -> BatchQualityPayload:
   789→   789→+    """Compute quality metrics for a single batch result."""
   790→   790→+    return {
   791→   791→+        "dimension_coverage": round(
   792→   792→+            len(assessments) / max(len(assessments), 1),
   793→   793→+            3,

   797→   797→+            / max(len(issues), 1),
   798→   798→+            3,

   800→   800→+        "high_score_missing_issue_note": high_score_missing_issue_note,

diff --git a/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/display_primitives.py b/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/display_primitives.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..702f7d4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/display_primitives.py
@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+"""Shared triage display primitives used by multiple rendering modules."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
+from desloppify.engine._plan.triage_playbook import (
+    TRIAGE_CMD_CLUSTER_ENRICH_COMPACT,
+    TRIAGE_STAGE_DEPENDENCIES,
+    TRIAGE_STAGE_LABELS,
+)
+
+from .helpers import manual_clusters_with_issues
+from .stage_helpers import unenriched_clusters
+
+
+def print_stage_progress(stages: dict, plan: dict | None = None) -> None:
+    """Print the triage-stage progress indicator."""
+    print(colorize("  Stages:", "dim"))
+    for stage_name, label in TRIAGE_STAGE_LABELS:
+        if stage_name in stages:
+            if stages[stage_name].get("confirmed_at"):
+                print(colorize(f"    ✓ {label} (confirmed)", "green"))
+            else:
+                print(colorize(f"    ✓ {label} (needs confirm)", "yellow"))
+        elif TRIAGE_STAGE_DEPENDENCIES[stage_name].issubset(stages):
+            print(colorize(f"    → {label} (current)", "yellow"))
+        else:
+            print(colorize(f"    ○ {label}", "dim"))
+
+    if plan and "reflect" in stages and "organize" not in stages:
+        gaps = unenriched_clusters(plan)
+        manual = manual_clusters_with_issues(plan)
+        if not manual:
+            print(colorize("\n    No manual clusters yet. Create clusters and enrich them.", "yellow"))
+        elif gaps:
+            print(colorize(f"\n    {len(gaps)} cluster(s) need enrichment:", "yellow"))
+            for name, missing in gaps:
+                print(colorize(f"      {name}: missing {', '.join(missing)}", "yellow"))
+            print(colorize(f"      Fix: {TRIAGE_CMD_CLUSTER_ENRICH_COMPACT}", "dim"))
+        else:
+            print(colorize(f"\n    All {len(manual)} manual cluster(s) enriched.", "green"))
+
+
+__all__ = ["print_stage_progress"]

+def _is_full_stage_run(stages_to_run: list[str]) -> bool:

+    *,

+    """True when each requested stage is confirmed or already confirmed."""

+"""Neutral detector datatypes shared across engine and language framework."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FunctionInfo:
+    """Extracted function/method info for cross-language analysis."""
+
+    name: str
+    file: str
+    line: int
+    end_line: int
+    loc: int
+    body: str
+    normalized: str = ""
+    body_hash: str = ""
+    params: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    return_annotation: str | None = None
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ClassInfo:
+    """Extracted class/component info for cross-language analysis."""
+
+    name: str
+    file: str
+    line: int
+    loc: int
+    methods: list[FunctionInfo] = field(default_factory=list)
+    attributes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    base_classes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    metrics: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ComplexitySignal:
+    """A complexity signal to detect in source files."""
+
+    name: str
+    pattern: str | None = None
+    weight: int = 1
+    threshold: int = 0
+    compute: Callable | None = None
+
+
+@dataclass
+class GodRule:
+    """A rule for detecting god classes/components."""
+
+    name: str
+    description: str
+    extract: Callable
+    threshold: int
+
+
+ELEVATED_PARAMS_THRESHOLD = 8
+ELEVATED_NESTING_THRESHOLD = 6
+ELEVATED_LOC_THRESHOLD = 300
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "ClassInfo",
+    "ComplexitySignal",
+    "ELEVATED_LOC_THRESHOLD",
+    "ELEVATED_NESTING_THRESHOLD",
+    "ELEVATED_PARAMS_THRESHOLD",
+    "FunctionInfo",
+    "GodRule",
+]

@@ -0,0 +1,155 @@
+"""Dependency wiring adapter for review batch execution core."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from ..runner_parallel import BatchExecutionOptions
+from ..runner_process import CodexBatchRunnerDeps, FollowupScanDeps
+
+
+def build_execution_adapter_kwargs(
+    *,
+    args,
+    policy,
+    runtime_project_root: Path,
+    subagent_runs_dir: Path,
+    run_stamp_fn,
+    load_or_prepare_packet_fn,
+    selected_batch_indexes_fn_raw,
+    parse_batch_selection_fn,
+    prepare_run_artifacts_fn_raw,
+    build_prompt_fn,
+    run_codex_batch_fn_raw,
+    execute_batches_fn,
+    collect_batch_results_fn_raw,
+    extract_payload_fn,
+    normalize_batch_result_fn,
+    max_batch_issues_for_dimension_count_fn,
+    print_failures_fn,
+    print_failures_and_raise_fn,
+    merge_batch_results_fn,
+    build_import_provenance_fn,
+    do_import_fn,
+    run_followup_scan_fn_raw,
+    safe_write_text_fn,
+    colorize_fn,
+    log_fn,
+    abstraction_sub_axes: tuple[str, ...],
+    followup_scan_timeout_seconds: int,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Build kwargs that adapt CLI/runtime wiring to execution.do_run_batches."""
+    batch_timeout_seconds = policy.batch_timeout_seconds
+    batch_max_retries = policy.batch_max_retries
+    batch_retry_backoff_seconds = policy.batch_retry_backoff_seconds
+    batch_heartbeat_seconds = policy.heartbeat_seconds
+    batch_live_log_interval_seconds = (
+        max(1.0, min(batch_heartbeat_seconds, 10.0))
+        if batch_heartbeat_seconds > 0
+        else 5.0
+    )
+    batch_stall_kill_seconds = policy.stall_kill_seconds
+
+    def _prepare_run_artifacts(*, stamp, selected_indexes, batches, packet_path, run_root, repo_root):
+        return prepare_run_artifacts_fn_raw(
+            stamp=stamp,
+            selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
+            batches=batches,
+            packet_path=packet_path,
+            run_root=run_root,
+            repo_root=repo_root,
+            build_prompt_fn=build_prompt_fn,
+            safe_write_text_fn=safe_write_text_fn,
+            colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
+        )
+
+    def _collect_batch_results(*, selected_indexes, failures, output_files, allowed_dims):
+        return collect_batch_results_fn_raw(
+            selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
+            failures=failures,
+            output_files=output_files,
+            allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
+            extract_payload_fn=lambda raw: extract_payload_fn(raw, log_fn=log_fn),
+            normalize_result_fn=lambda payload, dims: normalize_batch_result_fn(
+                payload,
+                dims,
+                max_batch_issues=max_batch_issues_for_dimension_count_fn(len(dims)),
+                abstraction_sub_axes=abstraction_sub_axes,
+            ),
+        )
+
+    return {
+        "run_stamp_fn": run_stamp_fn,
+        "load_or_prepare_packet_fn": load_or_prepare_packet_fn,
+        "selected_batch_indexes_fn": (
+            lambda _args, *, batch_count: selected_batch_indexes_fn_raw(
+                raw_selection=getattr(args, "only_batches", None),
+                batch_count=batch_count,
+                parse_fn=parse_batch_selection_fn,
+                colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
+            )
+        ),
+        "prepare_run_artifacts_fn": _prepare_run_artifacts,
+        "run_codex_batch_fn": (
+            lambda *, prompt, repo_root, output_file, log_file: run_codex_batch_fn_raw(
+                prompt=prompt,
+                repo_root=repo_root,
+                output_file=output_file,
+                log_file=log_file,
+                deps=CodexBatchRunnerDeps(
+                    timeout_seconds=batch_timeout_seconds,
+                    subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
+                    timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
+                    safe_write_text_fn=safe_write_text_fn,
+                    use_popen_runner=(getattr(subprocess.run, "__module__", "") == "subprocess"),
+                    subprocess_popen=subprocess.Popen,
+                    live_log_interval_seconds=batch_live_log_interval_seconds,
+                    stall_after_output_seconds=batch_stall_kill_seconds,
+                    max_retries=batch_max_retries,
+                    retry_backoff_seconds=batch_retry_backoff_seconds,
+                ),
+            )
+        ),
+        "execute_batches_fn": (
+            lambda **kwargs: execute_batches_fn(
+                tasks=kwargs["tasks"],
+                options=BatchExecutionOptions(
+                    run_parallel=kwargs["options"].run_parallel,
+                    max_parallel_workers=kwargs["options"].max_parallel_workers,
+                    heartbeat_seconds=kwargs["options"].heartbeat_seconds,
+                ),
+                progress_fn=kwargs.get("progress_fn"),
+                error_log_fn=kwargs.get("error_log_fn"),
+            )
+        ),
+        "collect_batch_results_fn": _collect_batch_results,
+        "print_failures_fn": print_failures_fn,
+        "print_failures_and_raise_fn": print_failures_and_raise_fn,
+        "merge_batch_results_fn": merge_batch_results_fn,
+        "build_import_provenance_fn": build_import_provenance_fn,
+        "do_import_fn": do_import_fn,
+        "run_followup_scan_fn": (
+            lambda *, lang_name, scan_path: run_followup_scan_fn_raw(
+                lang_name=lang_name,
+                scan_path=scan_path,
+                deps=FollowupScanDeps(
+                    project_root=runtime_project_root,
+                    timeout_seconds=followup_scan_timeout_seconds,
+                    python_executable=sys.executable,
+                    subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
+                    timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
+                    colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
+                ),
+            )
+        ),
+        "safe_write_text_fn": safe_write_text_fn,
+        "colorize_fn": colorize_fn,
+        "project_root": runtime_project_root,
+        "subagent_runs_dir": subagent_runs_dir,
+    }
+
+
+__all__ = ["build_execution_adapter_kwargs"]

+"""Shared degraded-plan warning helpers for resolve flows."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import sys
+
+from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
+
+_warned_degraded_mode = False
+
+
+def warn_plan_load_degraded_once(*, error_kind: str | None, behavior: str) -> None:
+    """Print one consistent warning when resolve behavior degrades."""
+    global _warned_degraded_mode
+    if _warned_degraded_mode:
+        return
+    _warned_degraded_mode = True
+
+    detail = f" ({error_kind})" if error_kind else ""
+    print(
+        colorize(
+            "  Warning: resolve is running in degraded mode because the living "
+            f"plan could not be loaded{detail}.",
+            "yellow",
+        ),
+        file=sys.stderr,
+    )
+    print(
+        colorize(f"  {behavior}", "dim"),
+        file=sys.stderr,
+    )
+
+
+def _reset_degraded_plan_warning_for_tests() -> None:
+    """Test helper to reset warning dedupe state."""
+    global _warned_degraded_mode
+    _warned_degraded_mode = False
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "warn_plan_load_degraded_once",
+]

+def _parse_heartbeat_details(
+    details: dict[str, object],
+) -> tuple[list[int], list[int], dict[int, float]]:
+    """Normalize heartbeat payload fields into typed active/queued/elapsed collections."""
+    raw_active = details.get("active_batches")
+    raw_queued = details.get("queued_batches")
+    raw_elapsed = details.get("elapsed_seconds")
+
+    active = [idx for idx in raw_active if isinstance(idx, int)] if isinstance(raw_active, list) else []
+    queued = [idx for idx in raw_queued if isinstance(idx, int)] if isinstance(raw_queued, list) else []
+
+    elapsed: dict[int, float] = {}
+    if isinstance(raw_elapsed, dict):
+        for idx, seconds in raw_elapsed.items():
+            if not isinstance(idx, int):
+                continue
+            if not isinstance(seconds, int | float):
+                continue
+            elapsed[idx] = float(seconds)
+    return active, queued, elapsed
+
+
+def _render_heartbeat_segments(
+    *,
+    active: list[int],
+    elapsed_seconds: dict[int, float],
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Render per-batch elapsed segments for heartbeat output."""
+    segments: list[str] = []
+    for idx in active[:6]:
+        seconds = int(elapsed_seconds.get(idx, 0.0))
+        segments.append(f"#{idx + 1}:{seconds}s")
+    if len(active) > 6:
+        segments.append(f"+{len(active) - 6} more")
+    return segments
+
+
+def _find_newly_stalled_batches(
+    *,
+    active: list[int],
+    elapsed_seconds: dict[int, float],
+    stall_warning_seconds: float,
+    stall_warned_batches: set[int],
+) -> list[int]:
+    """Return active batches that crossed the stall threshold for the first time."""
+    if stall_warning_seconds <= 0:
+        return []
+    return [
+        idx
+        for idx in active
+        if int(elapsed_seconds.get(idx, 0.0)) >= stall_warning_seconds
+        and idx not in stall_warned_batches
+    ]
+

+def _is_dataclass_decorator(decorator: ast.AST) -> bool:
+    """Return True when decorator is ``@dataclass`` (name or call form)."""
+    return (
+        isinstance(decorator, ast.Name)
+        and decorator.id == "dataclass"
+    ) or (
+        isinstance(decorator, ast.Call)
+        and isinstance(decorator.func, ast.Name)
+        and decorator.func.id == "dataclass"
+    )
+
+
+def _dataclass_init_node_ids(
+    tree: ast.Module,
+    *,
+    all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None = None,
+) -> set[int]:
+    """Collect __init__ function node IDs that belong to dataclass classes."""
+    init_ids: set[int] = set()
+    for class_node in _iter_nodes(tree, all_nodes, ast.ClassDef):
+        if not any(_is_dataclass_decorator(dec) for dec in class_node.decorator_list):
+            continue
+        for class_item in class_node.body:
+            if isinstance(class_item, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and class_item.name == "__init__":
+                init_ids.add(id(class_item))
+    return init_ids
+

Now I have a complete picture. Here is my audit.

---

## Audit of Uncommitted Changes

### Summary: 15 files changed, -820/+624 lines (net -196). Mostly good changes.

---

### 1. `desloppify/engine/_plan/sync_dimensions.py` -- **Good**

Core bug fix. Permanently-skipped unscored subjective dimensions were never being resurfaced for initial review. The fix:
- Adds `_skipped_subjective_ids()` helper to find skipped subjective IDs.
- Adds `_prune_skipped_subjective_ids()` to repair queue/skipped overlap invariants.
- In `sync_unscored_dimensions()`: clears skip entries for unscored IDs (they've never been scored, so a permanent skip is premature) and records them in `result.resurfaced`.
- In `sync_stale_dimensions()`: filters skipped IDs out of `injectable_ids` and repairs overlap.

Logic is clean and well-commented. Correctly handles the edge case where an unscored dimension was prematurely skipped.

### 2. `desloppify/engine/_plan/constants.py` -- **Good**

Adds `resurfaced: list[str]` field to `QueueSyncResult` dataclass, and includes it in the `changes` property. Direct support for the sync_dimensions fix above.

### 3. `desloppify/app/commands/scan/plan_reconcile.py` -- **Good**

- Prints a message when resurfaced dimensions are detected (user-facing feedback for the new behavior).
- Tightens `runtime` parameter type from `Any` to `ScanRuntime` (using `TYPE_CHECKING` import). Minor but correct improvement.
- Removes `runtime.state["_plan_reconcile_save_failed"] = True` -- no remaining references confirm this was dead code.

### 4. `desloppify/engine/_plan/auto_cluster_sync.py` -- **Good**

Prevents skipped subjective IDs from being re-queued by auto-clustering. Adds `_skipped_subjective_ids()` (duplicated from sync_dimensions.py -- see note below), filters them from `under_target_ids`, and removes overlapping entries from `queue_order`.

**Minor concern**: `_skipped_subjective_ids()` is defined identically in both `sync_dimensions.py` and `auto_cluster_sync.py`. Could be extracted to a shared helper. Not a blocking issue -- the function is small (8 lines) and both modules operate independently.

### 5. `desloppify/app/commands/plan/_resolve.py` -- **Good**

Adds glob/prefix matching against plan IDs (skipped, queued, clustered) before falling back to queue ID matching. Six clean lines. Fills a gap where patterns like `subjective::*` wouldn't match plan-level IDs.

### 6. `desloppify/app/commands/plan/override_skip.py` -- **Good with reservations**

Two additions:

**Deferral attestation (lines 108-145)**: When `--confirm` is used with a temporary skip, requires `--reason` and an `--attest` string containing specific phrases ("i have actually reflected", "not deferring"). This is an intentional friction mechanism to prevent lazy deferral.

- Assessment: The concept is sound (preventing thoughtless deferrals), but requiring exact magic phrases feels **slightly over-engineered**. A simpler `--attest` flag (boolean) + mandatory `--reason` would achieve 90% of the same effect with less user friction. That said, this is a deliberate design choice for a tool that coaches behavior, so it's defensible.

**Wontfix hint (lines 213-220)**: After a temporary skip succeeds, prints a suggestion to use `--permanent` if the user doesn't actually plan to fix the items. Helpful nudge -- **good**.

### 7. `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_flow_enrich_sense.py` (deleted) -- **Good**

This was a pure re-export shim. Per the project's backward compatibility policy, re-export facades should be removed. The imports in `stage_flow_commands.py` are updated to point directly at `stage_flow_enrich` and `stage_flow_sense_check`.

### 8. `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_flow_commands.py` -- **Good (Neutral)**

Updates imports to point at the real modules after the shim removal above. Mechanical, correct.

### 9. `desloppify/app/commands/review/_runner_parallel_loop.py` (deleted) + `runner_parallel.py` -- **Good**

348-line file deleted. No remaining importers. The file contained serial/parallel execution loop helpers. Grep confirms zero references remain.

`runner_parallel.py` also simplifies a pointless `write_back_failed` flag pattern -- the old code set a boolean, checked it, logged a debug message, then continued anyway. Now it just catches the exception and warns. Cleaner.

### 10. `desloppify/app/commands/review/batch/core_normalize.py` + `core_normalize_logic.py` (deleted) -- **Good (Neutral)**

Inlines `core_normalize_logic.py` (414 lines) directly into `core_normalize.py`, which was previously just a re-export shim. The code is identical -- this is a pure structural collapse removing one level of indirection. Follows the backward compat policy.

### 11. Test files -- **Good**

- `test_triage_stage_prompts_flow_direct.py`: Updates imports to match the shim removal. Mechanical.
- `test_auto_cluster_sync_direct.py`: Adds a test verifying skipped under-target IDs don't get re-queued. Good coverage for the auto_cluster_sync fix.
- `test_stale_dimensions.py`: Adds two tests -- one for resurfacing skipped unscored IDs, one for repairing skipped/queue overlap. Good coverage for the sync_dimensions fix.

### 12. Files listed as modified but with no actual diff

`sync_triage.py`, `lifecycle.py`, `test_sync_split_modules_direct.py`, `test_epic_triage.py` -- these show as modified in `git status` but produce no diff against HEAD. They were likely touched and reverted. They won't affect anything.

---

### Overall Assessment

| Category | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Good (bug fix / real improvement) | 8 changes |
| Neutral (cleanup, follows policy) | 3 changes |
| Bad (overzealous / over-engineered) | 0 |

**One item worth discussing**: The deferral attestation magic-phrase mechanism in `override_skip.py` is the only change that leans toward over-engineering, but it's a deliberate friction design for a coaching tool, so it's defensible. Everything else is clean: the core sync_dimensions bug fix is correct and well-tested, the shim/facade removals follow project policy, and the dead code cleanup is verified safe (no remaining references).

   347→def _print_llm_header() -> None:

   361→def _load_living_plan_snapshot() -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
   362→    fallback: dict[str, object] = {
   363→        "queue_order": [],
   364→        "clusters": {},
   365→        "skipped": {},
   366→        "active_cluster": None,
   367→    }
   368→    try:
   369→        loaded_plan = load_plan()
   370→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   371→        return fallback, False
   372→    if not isinstance(loaded_plan, dict):
   373→        loaded_plan = {}
   374→    loaded_plan.setdefault("queue_order", [])
   375→    loaded_plan.setdefault("clusters", {})
   376→    loaded_plan.setdefault("skipped", {})
   377→    loaded_plan.setdefault("active_cluster", None)
   378→
   379→    queue_order = loaded_plan.get("queue_order")
   380→    clusters = loaded_plan.get("clusters")
   381→    skipped = loaded_plan.get("skipped")
   382→    active = loaded_plan.get("active_cluster")
   383→
   384→    snapshot = {
   385→        "queue_order": queue_order if isinstance(queue_order, list) else [],
   386→        "clusters": clusters if isinstance(clusters, dict) else {},
   387→        "skipped": skipped if isinstance(skipped, dict) else {},
   388→        "active_cluster": active if isinstance(active, str) and active else None,
   389→    }
   390→    has_plan = bool(snapshot["queue_order"] or snapshot["clusters"] or snapshot["skipped"])
   391→    return snapshot, has_plan
   392→
   393→
   394→def _print_living_plan_notice(plan_snapshot: dict[str, object]) -> None:
   395→    ordered = len(plan_snapshot.get("queue_order", []))
   396→    skipped = len(plan_snapshot.get("skipped", {}))
   397→    active = plan_snapshot.get("active_cluster")
   398→    print(f"LIVING PLAN ACTIVE: {ordered} ordered, {skipped} skipped.")
   399→    if isinstance(active, str) and active:
   400→        cluster = plan_snapshot.get("clusters", {}).get(active)
   401→        issue_ids = cluster.get("issue_ids", []) if isinstance(cluster, dict) else []
   402→        remaining = len(issue_ids) if isinstance(issue_ids, list) else 0
   403→        print(f"Focused on: {active} ({remaining} items remaining).")
   404→    print("The plan is the single source of truth for work order.")
   405→    print("Use `desloppify next` which respects the plan.")
   406→    print("Use `desloppify plan` to view and update it.\n")
   407→

   410→    """Auto-install or update the skill document if we detect an agent.
   411→
   412→    Called unconditionally from the scan workflow — not gated on scores.
   413→    """
   414→    if not is_agent_environment():
   415→        return
   416→
   417→    _try_auto_update_skill()
   418→
   419→    # Single post-check: whatever happened above, is the doc current now?
   420→    install = skill_docs_mod.find_installed_skill()
   421→    if not install:
   422→        names = ", ".join(sorted(skill_docs_mod.SKILL_TARGETS))
   423→        print(
   424→            f"No skill document found. Install one for better workflow guidance: "
   425→            f"desloppify update-skill <{names}>"
   426→        )
   427→    elif install.stale:

    10→from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root
    11→
    12→
    13→def matches_exclusion(rel_path: str, exclusion: str) -> bool:
    14→    """Check if a relative path matches an exclusion pattern."""
    15→    parts = Path(rel_path).parts
    16→    if exclusion in parts:
    17→        return True
    18→    if "*" in exclusion:
    19→        if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(part, exclusion) for part in parts):
    20→            return True
    21→        # Full-path glob match for patterns with directory separators
    22→        # (e.g. "Wan2GP/**" should match "Wan2GP/models/rf.py").
    23→        if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    24→            normalized_path = rel_path.lstrip("./")
    25→            if fnmatch.fnmatch(normalized_path, exclusion):
    26→                return True
    27→    if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    28→        normalized = exclusion.rstrip("/").rstrip(os.sep)
    29→        return rel_path == normalized or rel_path.startswith(normalized + "/") or rel_path.startswith(
    30→            normalized + os.sep
    31→        )
    32→    return False
    33→
    34→
    35→def normalize_path_separators(path: str) -> str:
    36→    return path.replace("\\", "/")
    37→
    38→
    39→def safe_relpath(path: str | Path, start: str | Path) -> str:
    40→    try:
    41→        return os.path.relpath(str(path), str(start))
    42→    except ValueError:
    43→        return str(Path(path).resolve())
    44→
    45→
    46→def to_project_relative_path(path: str | Path) -> str:
    47→    """Return a normalized project-relative path when possible."""
    48→    root = get_project_root()
    49→    resolved = Path(path).resolve()
    50→    try:
    51→        return normalize_path_separators(str(resolved.relative_to(root)))
    52→    except ValueError:
    53→        return normalize_path_separators(safe_relpath(resolved, root))
    54→
    55→
    56→def rel(path: str | Path) -> str:
    57→    """Compatibility alias for :func:`to_project_relative_path`."""
    58→    return to_project_relative_path(path)
    59→
    60→
    61→def resolve_path(filepath: str) -> str:
    62→    """Resolve a filepath to absolute, handling both relative and absolute."""
    63→    p = Path(filepath)
    64→    if p.is_absolute():
    65→        return str(p.resolve())
    66→    return str((get_project_root() / filepath).resolve())
    67→
    68→
    69→def resolve_scan_file(
    70→    filepath: str | Path,
    71→    *,
    72→    scan_root: str | Path | None = None,
    73→) -> Path:
    74→    """Resolve a scan file path with explicit scan-root-first semantics.
    75→
    76→    Relative file paths are resolved against ``scan_root`` first (when provided)
    77→    and then against the process project root as a fallback.
    78→    """
    79→    p = Path(filepath)
    80→    if p.is_absolute():
    81→        return p.resolve()
    82→
    83→    root = get_project_root()
    84→    if scan_root is not None:
    85→        scan_root_path = Path(scan_root)
    86→        scan_root_abs = (
    87→            scan_root_path.resolve()
    88→            if scan_root_path.is_absolute()
    89→            else (root / scan_root_path).resolve()
    90→        )
    91→        scan_candidate = (scan_root_abs / p).resolve()
    92→        if scan_candidate.exists():
    93→            return scan_candidate
    94→
    95→    return (root / p).resolve()
    96→
    97→

    12→def transitive_coverage(
    13→    directly_tested: set[str],
    14→    graph: dict,
    15→    production_files: set[str],
    16→) -> set[str]:
    17→    """BFS from directly-tested files through dep-graph imports."""
    18→    visited = set(directly_tested)
    19→    queue = deque(directly_tested)
    20→
    21→    while queue:
    22→        current = queue.popleft()
    23→        entry = graph.get(current)
    24→        if entry is None:
    25→            continue
    26→        for imported in entry.get("imports", set()):
    27→            if imported in production_files and imported not in visited:
    28→                visited.add(imported)
    29→                queue.append(imported)
    30→
    31→    return visited - directly_tested

    34→def analyze_test_quality(
    35→    test_files: set[str],
    36→    lang_name: str,
    37→    *,
    38→    load_lang_module: Callable[[str], object],
    39→    read_coverage_file_fn: Callable[..., Any],

    42→    """Analyze test quality per file using language-specific heuristics."""
    43→    mod = load_lang_module(lang_name)

    45→    mock_pats = list(getattr(mod, "MOCK_PATTERNS", []) or [])
    46→    snapshot_pats = list(getattr(mod, "SNAPSHOT_PATTERNS", []) or [])
    47→    test_func_re = getattr(mod, "TEST_FUNCTION_RE", None)
    48→    strip_comments = getattr(mod, "strip_comments", None)
    49→    placeholder_classifier = getattr(mod, "is_placeholder_test", None)
    50→
    51→    if test_func_re is None or not hasattr(test_func_re, "findall"):
    52→        import re
    53→
    54→        test_func_re = re.compile(r"$^")
    55→    if not callable(strip_comments):
    56→
    57→        def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
    58→            return text
    59→    if not callable(placeholder_classifier):
    60→
    61→        def placeholder_classifier(
    62→            _content: str, *, assertions: int, test_functions: int
    63→        ) -> bool:
    64→            _ = assertions
    65→            _ = test_functions
    66→            return False
    67→
    68→    quality_map: dict[str, dict] = {}
    69→
    70→    for test_path in test_files:
    71→        read_result = read_coverage_file_fn(
    72→            test_path,
    73→            context="coverage_quality_analysis",
    74→        )
    75→        if not read_result.ok:
    76→            continue
    77→        content = read_result.content
    78→
    79→        stripped = strip_comments(content)
    80→        lines = stripped.splitlines()
    81→
    82→        assertions = sum(
    83→            1 for line in lines if any(pat.search(line) for pat in assert_pats)
    84→        )
    85→        mocks = sum(1 for line in lines if any(pat.search(line) for pat in mock_pats))
    86→        snapshots = sum(
    87→            1 for line in lines if any(pat.search(line) for pat in snapshot_pats)
    88→        )
    89→        test_functions = len(test_func_re.findall(stripped))
    90→        try:
    91→            is_placeholder = bool(
    92→                placeholder_classifier(
    93→                    stripped,
    94→                    assertions=assertions,
    95→                    test_functions=test_functions,
    96→                )
    97→            )
    98→        except TypeError as exc:
    99→            logger.debug(
   100→                "Best-effort fallback failed while trying to classify placeholder "
   101→                "test quality for %s: %s",
   102→                test_path,
   103→                exc,
   104→            )
   105→            is_placeholder = False
   106→
   107→        if test_functions == 0:
   108→            quality = "no_tests"
   109→        elif assertions == 0:
   110→            quality = "assertion_free"
   111→        elif is_placeholder:
   112→            quality = "placeholder_smoke"
   113→        elif mocks > assertions:
   114→            quality = "over_mocked"
   115→        elif snapshots > 0 and snapshots > assertions * 0.5:
   116→            quality = "snapshot_heavy"
   117→        elif test_functions > 0 and assertions / test_functions < 1:
   118→            quality = "smoke"
   119→        elif assertions / test_functions >= 3:
   120→            quality = "thorough"
   121→        else:
   122→            quality = "adequate"
   123→
   124→        quality_map[test_path] = {

   129→            "placeholder": is_placeholder,

   136→def _build_prod_by_module(
   137→    production_files: set[str],
   138→    *,
   139→    project_root: str,
   140→) -> dict[str, str]:
   141→    """Build module lookup map for production files."""
   142→    root_str = project_root + os.sep
   143→    prod_by_module: dict[str, str] = {}
   144→    for prod_file in production_files:
   145→        rel_path = (
   146→            prod_file[len(root_str) :]
   147→            if prod_file.startswith(root_str)
   148→            else prod_file
   149→        )
   150→        module_name = rel_path.replace("/", ".").replace("\\", ".")
   151→        if "." in module_name:
   152→            module_name = module_name.rsplit(".", 1)[0]
   153→        prod_by_module[module_name] = prod_file
   154→        if module_name.endswith(".__init__"):
   155→            prod_by_module[module_name[: -len(".__init__")]] = prod_file
   156→        parts = module_name.split(".")
   157→        if parts:
   158→            prod_by_module[parts[-1]] = prod_file
   159→    return prod_by_module
   160→
   161→
   162→def get_test_files_for_prod(
   163→    prod_file: str,
   164→    test_files: set[str],
   165→    graph: dict,
   166→    lang_name: str,
   167→    parsed_imports_by_test: dict[str, set[str]] | None,
   168→    *,
   169→    parse_test_imports_fn: Callable[[str, set[str], dict[str, str], str], set[str]],
   170→    map_test_to_source_fn: Callable[[str, set[str], str], str | None],
   171→    project_root: str,
   172→) -> list[str]:
   173→    """Find which test files exercise a given production file."""
   174→    parsed_imports_by_test = parsed_imports_by_test or {}
   175→    root_str = project_root + os.sep
   176→    rel_prod = prod_file[len(root_str) :] if prod_file.startswith(root_str) else prod_file
   177→    module_name = rel_prod.replace("/", ".").replace("\\", ".")
   178→    if "." in module_name:
   179→        module_name = module_name.rsplit(".", 1)[0]
   180→    prod_by_module: dict[str, str] = {module_name: prod_file}
   181→    parts = module_name.split(".")
   182→    if parts:
   183→        prod_by_module[parts[-1]] = prod_file
   184→
   185→    result: list[str] = []
   186→    for test_path in test_files:
   187→        entry = graph.get(test_path)
   188→        if entry and prod_file in entry.get("imports", set()):
   189→            result.append(test_path)
   190→            continue
   191→        parsed = parsed_imports_by_test.get(test_path)
   192→        if parsed is None:
   193→            parsed = parse_test_imports_fn(
   194→                test_path,
   195→                {prod_file},
   196→                prod_by_module,
   197→                lang_name,
   198→            )
   199→        if prod_file in parsed:
   200→            result.append(test_path)
   201→            continue
   202→        if map_test_to_source_fn(test_path, {prod_file}, lang_name) == prod_file:
   203→            result.append(test_path)
   204→    return result
   205→
   206→
   207→def build_test_import_index(
   208→    test_files: set[str],
   209→    production_files: set[str],
   210→    lang_name: str,
   211→    *,
   212→    parse_test_imports_fn: Callable[[str, set[str], dict[str, str], str], set[str]],
   213→    project_root: str,
   214→) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
   215→    """Parse test import sources once, producing a test->production import index."""
   216→    prod_by_module = _build_prod_by_module(
   217→        production_files,
   218→        project_root=project_root,
   219→    )
   220→    index: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
   221→    for test_path in test_files:
   222→        index[test_path] = parse_test_imports_fn(
   223→            test_path,
   224→            production_files,
   225→            prod_by_module,
   226→            lang_name,
   227→        )
   228→    return index
   229→
   230→
   231→# Backward-compatible aliases for previous internal names.
   232→transitive_coverage_core = transitive_coverage
   233→analyze_test_quality_core = analyze_test_quality
   234→get_test_files_for_prod_core = get_test_files_for_prod
   235→build_test_import_index_core = build_test_import_index
   236→
   237→
   238→__all__ = [
   239→    "analyze_test_quality",
   240→    "analyze_test_quality_core",
   241→    "build_test_import_index",
   242→    "build_test_import_index_core",
   243→    "get_test_files_for_prod",
   244→    "get_test_files_for_prod_core",
   245→    "transitive_coverage",
   246→    "transitive_coverage_core",
   247→]

    12→def transitive_coverage(
    13→    directly_tested: set[str],
    14→    graph: dict,
    15→    production_files: set[str],
    16→) -> set[str]:
    17→    """BFS from directly-tested files through dep-graph imports."""
    18→    visited = set(directly_tested)
    19→    queue = deque(directly_tested)
    20→
    21→    while queue:
    22→        current = queue.popleft()
    23→        entry = graph.get(current)
    24→        if entry is None:
    25→            continue
    26→        for imported in entry.get("imports", set()):
    27→            if imported in production_files and imported not in visited:
    28→                visited.add(imported)
    29→                queue.append(imported)
    30→
    31→    return visited - directly_tested

    68→    quality_map: dict[str, dict] = {}
    69→
    70→    for test_path in test_files:
    71→        read_result = read_coverage_file_fn(
    72→            test_path,
    73→            context="coverage_quality_analysis",
    74→        )
    75→        if not read_result.ok:
    76→            continue
    77→        content = read_result.content
    78→
    79→        stripped = strip_comments(content)
    80→        lines = stripped.splitlines()
    81→
    82→        assertions = sum(
    83→            1 for line in lines if any(pat.search(line) for pat in assert_pats)
    84→        )
    85→        mocks = sum(1 for line in lines if any(pat.search(line) for pat in mock_pats))
    86→        snapshots = sum(
    87→            1 for line in lines if any(pat.search(line) for pat in snapshot_pats)
    88→        )
    89→        test_functions = len(test_func_re.findall(stripped))
    90→        try:
    91→            is_placeholder = bool(
    92→                placeholder_classifier(
    93→                    stripped,
    94→                    assertions=assertions,
    95→                    test_functions=test_functions,
    96→                )
    97→            )
    98→        except TypeError as exc:
    99→            logger.debug(
   100→                "Best-effort fallback failed while trying to classify placeholder "
   101→                "test quality for %s: %s",
   102→                test_path,
   103→                exc,
   104→            )
   105→            is_placeholder = False
   106→
   107→        if test_functions == 0:
   108→            quality = "no_tests"
   109→        elif assertions == 0:
   110→            quality = "assertion_free"
   111→        elif is_placeholder:
   112→            quality = "placeholder_smoke"
   113→        elif mocks > assertions:
   114→            quality = "over_mocked"
   115→        elif snapshots > 0 and snapshots > assertions * 0.5:
   116→            quality = "snapshot_heavy"
   117→        elif test_functions > 0 and assertions / test_functions < 1:
   118→            quality = "smoke"
   119→        elif assertions / test_functions >= 3:
   120→            quality = "thorough"
   121→        else:
   122→            quality = "adequate"
   123→
   124→        quality_map[test_path] = {
   125→            "assertions": assertions,
   126→            "mocks": mocks,
   127→            "test_functions": test_functions,
   128→            "snapshots": snapshots,
   129→            "placeholder": is_placeholder,
   130→            "quality": quality,
   131→        }
   132→
   133→    return quality_map
   134→
   135→
   136→def _build_prod_by_module(
   137→    production_files: set[str],
   138→    *,
   139→    project_root: str,
   140→) -> dict[str, str]:
   141→    """Build module lookup map for production files."""
   142→    root_str = project_root + os.sep
   143→    prod_by_module: dict[str, str] = {}
   144→    for prod_file in production_files:
   145→        rel_path = (
   146→            prod_file[len(root_str) :]
   147→            if prod_file.startswith(root_str)
   148→            else prod_file
   149→        )
   150→        module_name = rel_path.replace("/", ".").replace("\\", ".")
   151→        if "." in module_name:
   152→            module_name = module_name.rsplit(".", 1)[0]
   153→        prod_by_module[module_name] = prod_file
   154→        if module_name.endswith(".__init__"):
   155→            prod_by_module[module_name[: -len(".__init__")]] = prod_file
   156→        parts = module_name.split(".")
   157→        if parts:
   158→            prod_by_module[parts[-1]] = prod_file
   159→    return prod_by_module
   160→
   161→
   162→def get_test_files_for_prod(
   163→    prod_file: str,
   164→    test_files: set[str],
   165→    graph: dict,
   166→    lang_name: str,
   167→    parsed_imports_by_test: dict[str, set[str]] | None,
   168→    *,
   169→    parse_test_imports_fn: Callable[[str, set[str], dict[str, str], str], set[str]],
   170→    map_test_to_source_fn: Callable[[str, set[str], str], str | None],
   171→    project_root: str,
   172→) -> list[str]:
   173→    """Find which test files exercise a given production file."""
   174→    parsed_imports_by_test = parsed_imports_by_test or {}
   175→    root_str = project_root + os.sep
   176→    rel_prod = prod_file[len(root_str) :] if prod_file.startswith(root_str) else prod_file
   177→    module_name = rel_prod.replace("/", ".").replace("\\", ".")
   178→    if "." in module_name:
   179→        module_name = module_name.rsplit(".", 1)[0]
   180→    prod_by_module: dict[str, str] = {module_name: prod_file}
   181→    parts = module_name.split(".")
   182→    if parts:
   183→        prod_by_module[parts[-1]] = prod_file
   184→
   185→    result: list[str] = []
   186→    for test_path in test_files:
   187→        entry = graph.get(test_path)
   188→        if entry and prod_file in entry.get("imports", set()):
   189→            result.append(test_path)
   190→            continue
   191→        parsed = parsed_imports_by_test.get(test_path)
   192→        if parsed is None:
   193→            parsed = parse_test_imports_fn(
   194→                test_path,
   195→                {prod_file},
   196→                prod_by_module,
   197→                lang_name,
   198→            )
   199→        if prod_file in parsed:
   200→            result.append(test_path)
   201→            continue
   202→        if map_test_to_source_fn(test_path, {prod_file}, lang_name) == prod_file:
   203→            result.append(test_path)
   204→    return result
   205→
   206→
   207→def build_test_import_index(
   208→    test_files: set[str],
   209→    production_files: set[str],
   210→    lang_name: str,
   211→    *,
   212→    parse_test_imports_fn: Callable[[str, set[str], dict[str, str], str], set[str]],
   213→    project_root: str,
   214→) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
   215→    """Parse test import sources once, producing a test->production import index."""
   216→    prod_by_module = _build_prod_by_module(
   217→        production_files,
   218→        project_root=project_root,
   219→    )
   220→    index: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
   221→    for test_path in test_files:
   222→        index[test_path] = parse_test_imports_fn(
   223→            test_path,
   224→            production_files,
   225→            prod_by_module,
   226→            lang_name,
   227→        )
   228→    return index
   229→
   230→
   231→# Backward-compatible aliases for previous internal names.
   232→transitive_coverage_core = transitive_coverage
   233→analyze_test_quality_core = analyze_test_quality
   234→get_test_files_for_prod_core = get_test_files_for_prod
   235→build_test_import_index_core = build_test_import_index
   236→
   237→

   242→    "build_test_import_index_core",

   244→    "get_test_files_for_prod_core",
   245→    "transitive_coverage",
   246→    "transitive_coverage_core",
   247→]

    13→def matches_exclusion(rel_path: str, exclusion: str) -> bool:
    14→    """Check if a relative path matches an exclusion pattern."""
    15→    parts = Path(rel_path).parts
    16→    if exclusion in parts:
    17→        return True
    18→    if "*" in exclusion:
    19→        if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(part, exclusion) for part in parts):
    20→            return True
    21→        # Full-path glob match for patterns with directory separators
    22→        # (e.g. "Wan2GP/**" should match "Wan2GP/models/rf.py").
    23→        if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    24→            normalized_path = rel_path.lstrip("./")
    25→            if fnmatch.fnmatch(normalized_path, exclusion):
    26→                return True
    27→    if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    28→        normalized = exclusion.rstrip("/").rstrip(os.sep)
    29→        return rel_path == normalized or rel_path.startswith(normalized + "/") or rel_path.startswith(
    30→            normalized + os.sep
    31→        )

    48→    root = get_project_root()

    50→    try:
    51→        return normalize_path_separators(str(resolved.relative_to(root)))
    52→    except ValueError:

    74→    """Resolve a scan file path with explicit scan-root-first semantics.
    75→
    76→    Relative file paths are resolved against ``scan_root`` first (when provided)
    77→    and then against the process project root as a fallback.
    78→    """
    79→    p = Path(filepath)

    82→
    83→    root = get_project_root()

    86→        scan_root_abs = (

    88→            if scan_root_path.is_absolute()

   106→        os.replace(tmp, str(p))
   107→    except OSError:

    32→
    33→    print(colorize("\n  Desloppify Configuration\n", "bold"))
    34→    for key, schema in CONFIG_SCHEMA.items():
    35→        value = config.get(key, schema.default)

    38→        # Format display value

    49→        print(f"  {key:<25} {display}{default_tag}")

    71→        display = "never (0)"
    72→    print(colorize(f"  Set {key} = {display}", "green"))

    20→
    21→def _resolve_detector_key(
    22→    detector: str, detect_commands: dict[str, object]
    23→) -> str | None:
    24→    """Resolve detector input to a command key."""
    25→    detector = detector.strip()
    26→    if detector in detect_commands:
    27→        return detector
    28→
    29→    normalized = detector.lower().replace("-", "_")
    30→    if normalized in detect_commands:
    31→        return normalized
    32→
    33→    denormalized = detector.lower().replace("_", "-")
    34→    if denormalized in detect_commands:
    35→        return denormalized
    36→
    37→    return None
    38→
    39→
    40→def cmd_detect(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    41→    """Run a single detector directly (bypass state tracking)."""
    42→    detector_input = args.detector
    43→
    44→    # Resolve language (from --lang flag or auto-detection)
    45→    lang_cfg = resolve_lang(args)
    46→
    47→    if not lang_cfg:
    48→        langs = ", ".join(lang_api.available_langs()) or "registered language plugins"
    49→        raise CommandError(
    50→            f"No language specified. Use --lang <name> (available: {langs})."
    51→        )
    52→
    53→    # Validate detector name
    54→    detector = _resolve_detector_key(detector_input, lang_cfg.detect_commands)
    55→    if detector is None:
    56→        available = ", ".join(sorted(lang_cfg.detect_commands))
    57→        raise CommandError(
    58→            f"Unknown detector for {lang_cfg.name}: {detector_input}\n"
    59→            f"  Available: {available}"
    60→        )
    61→
    62→    # Set default thresholds for detectors that expect them
    63→    if getattr(args, "threshold", None) is None:
    64→        if detector == "large":
    65→            args.threshold = lang_cfg.large_threshold
    66→        elif detector == "dupes":
    67→            args.threshold = 0.8
    68→
    69→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
    70→    lang_settings = resolve_lang_settings(runtime.config, lang_cfg)
    71→    try:
    72→        lang_options = resolve_lang_runtime_options(args, lang_cfg)
    73→    except LangRuntimeOptionsError as exc:
    74→        print_lang_runtime_options_error(exc, lang_name=lang_cfg.name)
    75→        raise CommandError(str(exc), exit_code=2) from exc
    76→    lang = lang_runtime.make_lang_run(
    77→        lang_cfg,
    78→        overrides=lang_runtime.LangRunOverrides(
    79→            runtime_settings=lang_settings,
    80→            runtime_options=lang_options,
    81→        ),
    82→    )
    83→    args.lang_runtime_options = dict(lang_options)
    84→    try:
    85→        lang.detect_commands[detector](args)
    86→    finally:
    87→        args.lang_runtime_options = None
    88→    if not getattr(args, "json", False):
    89→        scan_path = getattr(args, "path", ".") or "."
    90→        print(
    91→            colorize(f"\n  Next command: `desloppify scan --path {scan_path}`", "dim"),
    92→            file=sys.stderr,
    93→        )
    94→

    29→def _normalize_lang_name(raw: str) -> str:
    30→    name = raw.strip().lower().replace("-", "_")
    31→    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*", name):
    32→        raise ValueError("language name must match [a-z][a-z0-9_]*")
    33→    if keyword.iskeyword(name):

    38→def _normalize_extensions(values: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    39→    out: list[str] = []
    40→    for val in values or []:
    41→        ext = val.strip()
    42→        if not ext:
    43→            continue
    44→        if not ext.startswith("."):
    45→            ext = "." + ext
    46→        if not re.fullmatch(r"\.[a-z0-9]+", ext):
    47→            raise ValueError(f"invalid extension: {val!r}")
    48→        out.append(ext)
    49→    if not out:
    50→        raise ValueError("at least one --extension is required")
    51→    seen: set[str] = set()
    52→    deduped: list[str] = []
    53→    for ext in out:
    54→        if ext not in seen:
    55→            seen.add(ext)
    56→            deduped.append(ext)

    93→def _append_toml_array_item(text: str, key: str, value: str) -> str:

    96→        re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL,

    98→    match = pattern.search(text)

   100→        return text
   101→

   103→    parsed = ast.literal_eval("[" + raw + "]") if raw else []
   104→    if not isinstance(parsed, list):

   111→    return text[: match.start()] + replacement + text[match.end() :]

   114→def _wire_pyproject(lang_name: str) -> bool:

   116→    if not pyproject_path.is_file():
   117→        return False
   118→
   119→    original = pyproject_path.read_text()
   120→    updated = original
   121→    updated = _append_toml_array_item(
   122→        updated,
   123→        "testpaths",
   124→        f"desloppify/languages/{lang_name}/tests",
   125→    )
   126→
   127→    if updated != original:
   128→        safe_write_text(pyproject_path, updated)
   129→        return True
   130→    return False
   131→
   132→
   133→def _cmd_scaffold_lang(args: object) -> None:
   134→    raw_name = getattr(args, "name", "")
   135→    lang_name = _normalize_lang_name(raw_name)
   136→    extensions = _normalize_extensions(getattr(args, "extension", None))
   137→    markers = _normalize_markers(getattr(args, "marker", None))
   138→    default_src = getattr(args, "default_src", "src") or "src"
   139→    force = bool(getattr(args, "force", False))
   140→    wire_pyproject = bool(getattr(args, "wire_pyproject", True))
   141→
   142→    lang_dir = get_project_root() / "desloppify" / "languages" / lang_name
   143→    if lang_dir.exists() and not force:
   144→        raise CommandError(
   145→            f"Language directory already exists: {lang_dir}. Use --force to overwrite."
   146→        )
   147→
   148→    files = _template_files(lang_name, extensions, markers, default_src)
   149→    for rel_path, content in files.items():
   150→        target = lang_dir / rel_path
   151→        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   152→        if target.exists() and not force:

   154→        safe_write_text(target, content)
   155→
   156→    wired = _wire_pyproject(lang_name) if wire_pyproject else False

    10→from desloppify import state as state_mod

    12→from desloppify.base import config as config_mod
    13→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import matches_exclusion
    14→from desloppify.base.exception_sets import PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS, CommandError
    15→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize

    21→    save_plan,
    22→)
    23→
    24→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    25→
    26→
    27→def _state_file_for_runtime(runtime) -> Path:
    28→    """Resolve the effective state file path for a command runtime."""
    29→    state_file = runtime.state_path
    30→    if isinstance(state_file, Path):
    31→        return state_file
    32→    return state_mod.get_state_file()
    33→
    34→
    35→def _prune_excluded_issues(state: dict, pattern: str) -> list[str]:
    36→    """Drop issues whose file path matches a new exclusion pattern."""
    37→    issues = state.get("issues")
    38→    if not isinstance(issues, dict):
    39→        return []
    40→
    41→    removed_ids = [
    42→        issue_id
    43→        for issue_id, issue in issues.items()
    44→        if isinstance(issue, dict)
    45→        and matches_exclusion(str(issue.get("file", "")), pattern)
    46→    ]
    47→    for issue_id in removed_ids:
    48→        issues.pop(issue_id, None)
    49→    return removed_ids
    50→
    51→
    52→def _purge_removed_ids_from_plan(state_file: Path, removed_ids: list[str]) -> int:
    53→    """Remove pruned issue IDs from queue/skips/clusters in plan.json."""
    54→    if not removed_ids:
    55→        return 0
    56→    plan_file = plan_path_for_state(state_file)
    57→    plan = load_plan(plan_file)
    58→    purged = purge_ids(plan, removed_ids)
    59→    if purged:
    60→        save_plan(plan, plan_file)
    61→    return purged
    62→
    63→
    64→def cmd_exclude(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    65→    """Add a path pattern to the exclude list and clean cached queue/state."""
    66→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
    67→    config = runtime.config
    68→    state = runtime.state
    69→    state_file = _state_file_for_runtime(runtime)
    70→
    71→    config_mod.add_exclude_pattern(config, args.pattern)
    72→    config["needs_rescan"] = True
    73→    try:
    74→        config_mod.save_config(config)
    75→    except OSError as exc:
    76→        raise CommandError(f"could not save config: {exc}") from exc
    77→
    78→    removed_ids: list[str] = []
    79→    plan_purged = 0
    80→    if state_file.exists():
    81→        removed_ids = _prune_excluded_issues(state, args.pattern)
    82→        if removed_ids:
    83→            try:
    84→                state_mod.save_state(state, state_file)
    85→            except OSError as exc:
    86→                raise CommandError(f"could not save state: {exc}") from exc
    87→
    88→            try:
    89→                plan_purged = _purge_removed_ids_from_plan(state_file, removed_ids)
    90→            except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
    91→                logger.debug("Exclude command could not update living plan.", exc_info=exc)
    92→                print(
    93→                    colorize("  Warning: could not update living plan.", "yellow"),
    94→                    file=sys.stderr,
    95→                )
    96→
    97→    print(colorize(f"Added exclude pattern: {args.pattern}", "green"))
    98→    if removed_ids:
    99→        print(f"  Removed {len(removed_ids)} matching issues from state.")
   100→        if plan_purged:
   101→            print(

   104→                    "dim",
   105→                )
   106→            )
   107→    config_warning = check_config_staleness(config)
   108→    if config_warning:
   109→        print(colorize(f"  {config_warning}", "yellow"))
   110→
   111→
   112→__all__ = ["cmd_exclude"]

1→"""langs command: list all available language plugins with depth and tools."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→import logging
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     9→from desloppify.languages._framework import registry_state
    10→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import LangConfig
    11→from desloppify.languages._framework.discovery import load_all
    12→from desloppify.languages._framework.generic import SHARED_PHASE_LABELS
    13→from desloppify.languages._framework.resolution import make_lang_config
    14→
    15→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    16→
    17→_DEPTH_BARS = {
    18→    "full": 8,
    19→    "standard": 5,
    20→    "shallow": 3,
    21→    "minimal": 2,
    22→}
    23→
    24→_DEPTH_MAX = 8
    25→
    26→
    27→def _depth_bar(depth: str) -> str:
    28→    """Render a depth bar like ████░░░░."""
    29→    filled = _DEPTH_BARS.get(depth, 2)
    30→    empty = _DEPTH_MAX - filled
    31→    return "\u2588" * filled + "\u2591" * empty
    32→
    33→
    34→def _get_tool_labels(cfg: LangConfig) -> str:
    35→    """Extract tool labels from phases."""
    36→    if cfg.integration_depth == "full":
    37→        return "custom detectors"
    38→    labels = [p.label for p in cfg.phases if p.label not in SHARED_PHASE_LABELS]
    39→    suffix = " (auto-fix)" if cfg.fixers else ""
    40→    return (", ".join(labels) if labels else "none") + suffix
    41→
    42→
    43→def cmd_langs(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    44→    """List all available languages with depth and tool info."""
    45→    load_all()
    46→
    47→    configs: list[tuple[str, LangConfig]] = []
    48→    for name, obj in sorted(registry_state.all_items()):
    49→        if isinstance(obj, LangConfig):
    50→            configs.append((name, obj))
    51→        else:
    52→            try:
    53→                cfg = make_lang_config(name, obj)
    54→                configs.append((name, cfg))
    55→            except (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError, AttributeError) as exc:
    56→                logger.debug("Skipping unresolvable lang config %s: %s", name, exc)
    57→                continue
    58→
    59→    # Sort: full first, then standard, shallow, minimal; alphabetical within
    60→    depth_order = {"full": 0, "standard": 1, "shallow": 2, "minimal": 3}
    61→    configs.sort(key=lambda x: (depth_order.get(x[1].integration_depth, 9), x[0]))
    62→
    63→    # Column widths
    64→    name_width = max(len(name) for name, _ in configs) + 2 if configs else 14
    65→    name_width = max(name_width, 14)
    66→
    67→    print()
    68→    header = f"{'Language':<{name_width}}{'Depth':<14}Tools"
    69→    print(colorize(header, "bold"))
    70→    print("\u2500" * 60)
    71→
    72→    for name, cfg in configs:
    73→        depth = getattr(cfg, "integration_depth", "full")
    74→        bar = _depth_bar(depth)
    75→        tools = _get_tool_labels(cfg)
    76→        print(f"{name:<{name_width}}{bar}    {tools}")
    77→    print()
    78→

1→"""update-skill command: install or update the desloppify skill document."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→import urllib.error
     7→import urllib.request
     8→
     9→from desloppify.app.skill_docs import (
    10→    SKILL_BEGIN,
    11→    SKILL_END,
    12→    SKILL_TARGETS,
    13→    SKILL_VERSION,
    14→    SKILL_VERSION_RE,
    15→    SkillInstall,
    16→    find_installed_skill,
    17→)
    18→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import safe_write_text
    19→from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root
    20→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
    21→
    22→_RAW_BASE = (
    23→    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/peteromallet/desloppify/main/docs"
    24→)
    25→
    26→
    27→def _download(filename: str) -> str:
    28→    """Download a file from the desloppify docs directory on GitHub."""
    29→    url = f"{_RAW_BASE}/{filename}"
    30→    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=15) as resp:  # noqa: S310
    31→        return resp.read().decode("utf-8")
    32→
    33→
    34→def _build_section(skill_content: str, overlay_content: str | None) -> str:
    35→    """Assemble the complete skill section from downloaded parts."""
    36→    parts = [skill_content.rstrip()]
    37→    if overlay_content:
    38→        parts.append(overlay_content.rstrip())
    39→    return "\n\n".join(parts) + "\n"
    40→
    41→
    42→# Interfaces whose skill systems parse YAML frontmatter and require ``---``
    43→# to appear on the very first line of the file.
    44→_FRONTMATTER_FIRST_INTERFACES = frozenset({"amp", "codex"})
    45→
    46→
    47→def _ensure_frontmatter_first(content: str) -> str:
    48→    """Move YAML frontmatter to the top if HTML comments precede it.
    49→
    50→    Some skill systems (e.g. AMP) require ``---`` on line 1 for frontmatter
    51→    parsing.  SKILL.md ships with ``<!-- desloppify-begin -->`` and a version
    52→    comment before the ``---`` block.  This function relocates those HTML
    53→    comment lines to just after the closing ``---``.
    54→    """
    55→    lines = content.split("\n")
    56→
    57→    # Find the opening ``---``.
    58→    fm_start = None
    59→    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    60→        if line.strip() == "---":
    61→            fm_start = i
    62→            break
    63→    if fm_start is None or fm_start == 0:
    64→        return content  # already fine or no frontmatter
    65→
    66→    # Collect the HTML-comment lines that precede the frontmatter.
    67→    prefix_lines = lines[:fm_start]
    68→
    69→    # Find the closing ``---``.
    70→    fm_end = None
    71→    for i, line in enumerate(lines[fm_start + 1 :], fm_start + 1):
    72→        if line.strip() == "---":
    73→            fm_end = i
    74→            break
    75→    if fm_end is None:
    76→        return content  # malformed frontmatter, leave untouched
    77→
    78→    # Reassemble: frontmatter first, then the prefix lines, then the rest.
    79→    reordered = (
    80→        lines[fm_start : fm_end + 1]
    81→        + prefix_lines
    82→        + lines[fm_end + 1 :]
    83→    )
    84→    return "\n".join(reordered)
    85→
    86→
    87→def _replace_section(file_content: str, new_section: str) -> str:
    88→    """Replace the desloppify section in a shared file, preserving surrounding content.
    89→
    90→    Uses first ``<!-- desloppify-begin -->`` and last ``<!-- desloppify-end -->``
    91→    so the overlay (which also has an end marker) is captured correctly.
    92→    """
    93→    begin = file_content.find(SKILL_BEGIN)
    94→    end = file_content.rfind(SKILL_END)
    95→    if begin == -1 or end == -1:
    96→        # No section markers — append (first install into existing shared file).
    97→        return file_content.rstrip() + "\n\n" + new_section
    98→
    99→    before = file_content[:begin]
   100→    after = file_content[end + len(SKILL_END):]
   101→    before = before.rstrip() + "\n\n" if before.strip() else ""
   102→    after = "\n" + after.lstrip("\n") if after.strip() else "\n"
   103→    return before + new_section + after
   104→
   105→
   106→def resolve_interface(
   107→    explicit: str | None = None,
   108→    install: SkillInstall | None = None,
   109→) -> str | None:
   110→    """Resolve which interface to update.
   111→
   112→    Uses the explicit argument if given, otherwise infers from an existing
   113→    install's overlay marker or file path.
   114→    """
   115→    if explicit:
   116→        return explicit.lower()
   117→
   118→    if install is None:
   119→        install = find_installed_skill()
   120→    if not install:
   121→        return None
   122→
   123→    if install.overlay:
   124→        return install.overlay.lower()
   125→
   126→    for name, (target, _overlay, _ded) in SKILL_TARGETS.items():
   127→        if target == install.rel_path:
   128→            return name
   129→    return None
   130→
   131→
   132→def update_installed_skill(interface: str) -> bool:
   133→    """Download and install the skill document for the given interface.
   134→
   135→    Returns True on success, False on failure. Prints status messages.
   136→    """
   137→    target_rel, overlay_name, dedicated = SKILL_TARGETS[interface]
   138→    target_path = get_project_root() / target_rel
   139→
   140→    print(colorize(f"Downloading skill document ({interface})...", "dim"))
   141→    try:
   142→        skill_content = _download("SKILL.md")
   143→        overlay_content = _download(f"{overlay_name}.md") if overlay_name else None
   144→    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError) as exc:
   145→        print(colorize(f"Download failed: {exc}", "red"))
   146→        return False
   147→
   148→    if "desloppify-skill-version" not in skill_content:
   149→        print(colorize("Downloaded content doesn't look like a skill document.", "red"))
   150→        return False
   151→
   152→    new_section = _build_section(skill_content, overlay_content)
   153→    if interface in _FRONTMATTER_FIRST_INTERFACES:
   154→        new_section = _ensure_frontmatter_first(new_section)
   155→
   156→    target_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   157→    if dedicated:
   158→        result = new_section
   159→    elif target_path.is_file():
   160→        existing = target_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   161→        result = _replace_section(existing, new_section)
   162→    else:
   163→        result = new_section
   164→
   165→    safe_write_text(target_path, result)
   166→
   167→    version_match = SKILL_VERSION_RE.search(new_section)
   168→    version = version_match.group(1) if version_match else "?"
   169→    print(
   170→        colorize(
   171→            f"Updated {target_rel} (v{version}, tool expects v{SKILL_VERSION})",
   172→            "green",
   173→        )
   174→    )
   175→    return True
   176→
   177→
   178→def cmd_update_skill(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   179→    """Install or update the desloppify skill document."""
   180→    interface = resolve_interface(getattr(args, "interface", None))
   181→
   182→    if not interface:
   183→        print(colorize("No installed skill document found.", "yellow"))
   184→        print()
   185→        names = ", ".join(sorted(SKILL_TARGETS))
   186→        print(f"Install with: desloppify update-skill <{names}>")
   187→        return
   188→
   189→    if interface not in SKILL_TARGETS:
   190→        names = ", ".join(sorted(SKILL_TARGETS))
   191→        print(colorize(f"Unknown interface '{interface}'.", "red"))
   192→        print(f"Available: {names}")
   193→        return
   194→
   195→    update_installed_skill(interface)
   196→

    32→def _zone_show(args: argparse.Namespace):

    34→    state_file = state_path(args)

1→"""Shared triage display primitives used by multiple rendering modules."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     6→from desloppify.engine._plan.triage_playbook import (
     7→    TRIAGE_CMD_CLUSTER_ENRICH_COMPACT,
     8→    TRIAGE_STAGE_DEPENDENCIES,
     9→    TRIAGE_STAGE_LABELS,
    10→)
    11→
    12→from .helpers import manual_clusters_with_issues
    13→from .stage_helpers import unenriched_clusters
    14→
    15→
    16→def print_stage_progress(stages: dict, plan: dict | None = None) -> None:
    17→    """Print the triage-stage progress indicator."""
    18→    print(colorize("  Stages:", "dim"))
    19→    for stage_name, label in TRIAGE_STAGE_LABELS:
    20→        if stage_name in stages:
    21→            if stages[stage_name].get("confirmed_at"):
    22→                print(colorize(f"    ✓ {label} (confirmed)", "green"))
    23→            else:
    24→                print(colorize(f"    ✓ {label} (needs confirm)", "yellow"))
    25→        elif TRIAGE_STAGE_DEPENDENCIES[stage_name].issubset(stages):
    26→            print(colorize(f"    → {label} (current)", "yellow"))
    27→        else:
    28→            print(colorize(f"    ○ {label}", "dim"))
    29→
    30→    if plan and "reflect" in stages and "organize" not in stages:
    31→        gaps = unenriched_clusters(plan)
    32→        manual = manual_clusters_with_issues(plan)
    33→        if not manual:
    34→            print(colorize("\n    No manual clusters yet. Create clusters and enrich them.", "yellow"))
    35→        elif gaps:
    36→            print(colorize(f"\n    {len(gaps)} cluster(s) need enrichment:", "yellow"))
    37→            for name, missing in gaps:
    38→                print(colorize(f"      {name}: missing {', '.join(missing)}", "yellow"))
    39→            print(colorize(f"      Fix: {TRIAGE_CMD_CLUSTER_ENRICH_COMPACT}", "dim"))
    40→        else:
    41→            print(colorize(f"\n    All {len(manual)} manual cluster(s) enriched.", "green"))
    42→
    43→
    44→__all__ = ["print_stage_progress"]
    45→

It accepted 30+ parameters, wrapped them in lambdas/closures for partial application, and returned a dict.     84→def _try_load_prepared_packet() -> dict | None:
    85→    """Load a prepared holistic packet from query.json if it looks valid.
    86→
    87→    Returns the packet dict when query.json exists, parses as JSON, and
    88→    contains the ``investigation_batches`` key written by ``--prepare``.
    89→    Returns ``None`` otherwise (missing file, parse error, wrong shape).
    90→    """
    91→    try:
    92→        qf = query_file_path()
    93→        if not qf.exists():
    94→            return None
    95→        data = json.loads(qf.read_text())
    96→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, RuntimeError):
    97→        return None
    98→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    99→        return None
   100→    if "investigation_batches" not in data:
   101→        return None
   102→    batches = data["investigation_batches"]
   103→    if not isinstance(batches, list) or not batches:
   104→        return None
   105→    return data
   106→

   108→def _merge_batch_results(batch_results: list[object]) -> dict[str, object]:
   109→    """Deterministically merge assessments/issues across batch outputs."""
   110→    normalized_results: list[BatchResultPayload] = []
   111→    for result in batch_results:
   112→        if hasattr(result, "to_dict") and callable(result.to_dict):
   113→            payload = result.to_dict()
   114→            if isinstance(payload, dict):
   115→                normalized_results.append(cast(BatchResultPayload, payload))
   116→                continue
   117→        if isinstance(result, dict):
   118→            normalized_results.append(cast(BatchResultPayload, result))
   119→    return merge_batch_results(
   120→        normalized_results,
   121→        abstraction_sub_axes=ABSTRACTION_SUB_AXES,
   122→        abstraction_component_names=ABSTRACTION_COMPONENT_NAMES,
   123→    )

   126→def _load_or_prepare_packet(

   134→    """Load packet override or prepare a fresh packet snapshot."""
   135→    packet_override = getattr(args, "packet", None)

   140→        try:

   144→        blind_path = _blind_packet_path()

   149→        return packet, packet_path, blind_path
   150→
   151→    # When no explicit --packet and no explicit --dimensions were given,
   152→    # check whether a prior ``review --prepare`` left a valid query.json
   153→    # packet we can reuse instead of rebuilding from scratch.
   154→    dims = parse_dimensions(args)

   162→            packet_path, blind_saved = write_packet_snapshot(

   170→            print(colorize(f"  Blind packet: {blind_saved}", "dim"))
   171→            return prepared, packet_path, blind_saved
   172→
   173→    path = Path(args.path)
